    test("3f's writers (0027_orders; design, section 6.7): who writes a decision's informed_at, an order's row, its events, an item's closing and a measure's withholding", async () => {
      const all = await functions();
      const writing = (pattern: RegExp) => all.filter((f) => pattern.test(f.definition)).map((f) => f.name);
      // A decision's informed_at: decisions_record forces it at the insert; order_correct writes it, and only to null; and
      // (Task 3, 0028_orders_ledger) order_notices_release tells a held decision, while the two later writers of a
      // decision's mail (decisions_apply's ended seals, decision_actions_check's step 11) hold a telling on a held post.
      expect(writing(/[^a-z_]informed_at (:)?= /)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_check", "public.decisions_apply", "public.decisions_record", "public.order_correct", "public.order_notices_release"]);
      expect(all.find((f) => f.name === "public.order_notices_release")!.definition).toContain("SET informed_at = clock_timestamp(), author_mail = 'pending'");
      expect(all.find((f) => f.name === "public.order_correct")!.definition).toMatch(/SET informed_at = NULL, author_mail = 'none'/);
      // An order's row: written by order_event_record and order_correct alone (and the command line, as the migrator).
      // Task 4 (0029_orders_retention): erase_order_records deletes it with its events and items once its records are due.
      expect(writing(/(UPDATE|INSERT INTO|DELETE FROM) public[.]legal_orders /i)).toEqual(["public.erase_order_records", "public.order_correct", "public.order_event_record"]);
      // Task 3: the ledger's events (effect_given, reinstated) and the release's notice_released.
      // Task 4: the end of a preservation's preservation_ended, by the system.
      expect(writing(/INSERT INTO public[.]legal_order_events/i)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.order_correct", "public.order_event_record", "public.order_notices_release", "public.order_preservation_end"]);
      // An item's closing: order_correct closes it; an effect clears it (decision_actions_apply).
      expect(writing(/closed_reason = /)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.order_correct"]);
      // An item's preservation (design, section 6.7): set and ended by the ledger (decision_actions_apply) and a correction
      // (order_correct), and ended by time by order_preservation_end (Task 4, 0029) alone.
      expect(writing(/preserve_(until|ended_at) = /)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.order_correct", "public.order_preservation_end"]);
      expect(writing(/withhold_author = /)).toEqual(["public.order_correct"]);
      // The two definer functions pin public alone and name auth's table in full, as every function the migrator owns does.
      for (const name of ["public.order_correct", "public.order_event_record", "public.legal_order_events_confirmed"]) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect([f.definer, f.config], name).toEqual([true, ["search_path=public, pg_temp"]]);
      }
      // No function of 0027 holds an interval literal or a number of order_rules(): each is read from there.
      // Nor any of 0029_orders_retention.
      for (const name of ["public.order_hold_end", "public.order_hold_until", "public.order_preserve_until", "public.order_event_record", "public.order_correct", "public.legal_orders_insert",
                          "public.order_preservation_end", "public.order_records_due", "public.erase_order_records", "public.delete_contact_messages"]) {
        expect(all.find((f) => f.name === name)!.definition, name).not.toMatch(/interval '/i);
      }
      const views = (await otherDefinitions()).filter((d) => d.kind === "view" && d.name === "legal_order_clock");
      expect(views.map((v) => /interval '/i.test(v.definition))).toEqual([false]);
    });

    test("3d Task 3 (0035_edge_purges; design, sections 6.3 and 6.9): only the two trigger functions insert into edge_purges, each a definer that compares through text; the API's role reads, moves four columns and deletes, and inserts nothing; both CHECKs are their constants", async () => {
      const all = await functions();
      // As pg_get_functiondef prints a statement: one space between words, the name schema-qualified or bare.
      const inserting = all.filter((f) => /insert into (only )?(public[.])?"?edge_purges"?[ (]/i.test(f.definition)).map((f) => f.name);
      expect(inserting).toEqual(["public.post_media_purge", "public.posts_purge"]);
      for (const name of ["public.post_media_purge", "public.posts_purge", "public.edge_purges_insert"]) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect({ owner: f.owner, definer: f.definer, config: f.config, api: f.api, pub: f.pub }, name).toEqual({
          owner: "korbat_migrate",
          definer: name !== "public.edge_purges_insert",
          config: ["search_path=public, pg_temp"],
          api: false,
          pub: false,
        });
        // Through text, never an enum literal: a level or a state added later is covered without being named.
        expect(f.definition, name).not.toMatch(/'[a-z_]+'::(public[.])?(post_state|moderation_level|media_moderation_state|media_status)/);
      }
      // Neither function takes a lock: no FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE or LOCK statement.
      for (const name of ["public.post_media_purge", "public.posts_purge"]) expect(all.find((f) => f.name === name)!.definition, name).not.toMatch(/ for (no key )?(update|share)| lock table /i);
      expect(await tablePrivileges("korbat_api", "public.edge_purges")).toEqual(["SELECT", "DELETE"]);
      expect(await updatableColumns("korbat_api", "public.edge_purges")).toEqual(["next_at", "attempts", "outcome", "done_at"]);
      const listed = (definition: string) => [...definition.matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
      expect(listed(await checkDefinition("edge_purges", "edge_purges_cause"))).toEqual([...EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES]);
      expect(listed(await checkDefinition("edge_purges", "edge_purges_outcome"))).toEqual([...EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES]);
      const [seq] = await apiDb.execute<{ usage: boolean }>(sql`select has_sequence_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.edge_purges_id_seq', 'USAGE') as usage`);
      expect(seq!.usage).toBe(false);
    });

    test("3d Task 6 (0038_automated_decisions; design, section 6.6): automation_rules() is AUTOMATION_RULES; the API's role reads and inserts a signal and sets four columns of it, reads and inserts a request for a person, and calls none of the three trigger functions; both CHECKs of a signal are their constants", async () => {
      const [row] = await apiDb.execute<Record<string, unknown>>(sql`select * from public.automation_rules()`);
      const camel = (name: string) => name.replace(/_([a-z])/g, (_m, letter: string) => letter.toUpperCase());
      expect(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(row!).map(([name, value]) => [camel(name), value === null ? null : Number(value)]))).toEqual({ ...AUTOMATION_RULES });
      expect(await tablePrivileges("korbat_api", "public.automated_signals")).toEqual(["SELECT", "INSERT"]);
      expect(await updatableColumns("korbat_api", "public.automated_signals")).toEqual(["intake_item_id", "decision_id", "handled_at", "handled"]);
      expect(await tablePrivileges("korbat_api", "public.automated_objections")).toEqual(["SELECT", "INSERT"]);
      expect(await updatableColumns("korbat_api", "public.automated_objections")).toEqual([]);
      const all = await functions();
      // The request's trigger is a definer: it reads the measures in force, which the API's role reads too, and refuses as
      // objection_not_open, so no caller learns more than that.
      for (const [name, definer] of [
        ["public.automated_signals_insert", false],
        ["public.automated_signals_guard", false],
        ["public.automated_objections_insert", true],
      ] as const) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect({ owner: f.owner, definer: f.definer, config: f.config, api: f.api, pub: f.pub }, name).toEqual({ owner: "korbat_migrate", definer, config: ["search_path=public, pg_temp"], api: false, pub: false });
      }
      const listed = (definition: string) => [...definition.matchAll(/'([a-z_0-9]+)'/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
      expect(listed(await checkDefinition("automated_signals", "automated_signals_kind"))).toEqual([...SIGNAL_KINDS]);
      expect(listed(await checkDefinition("automated_signals", "automated_signals_handled"))).toEqual([...SIGNAL_HANDLED]);
    });

    test("3f Task 5's writers (0030_authority_records; design, section 6.7): only report_open and report_close_unsealed write a hold and a notification record, erase_authority_records deletes them, and none holds a number of order_rules()", async () => {
      const all = await functions();
      const writing = (pattern: RegExp) => all.filter((f) => pattern.test(f.definition)).map((f) => f.name);
      expect(writing(/(UPDATE|INSERT INTO) auth[.]report_holds/i)).toEqual(["public.report_close_unsealed", "public.report_open"]);
      expect(writing(/(UPDATE|INSERT INTO) public[.]authority_notifications /i)).toEqual(["public.report_close_unsealed", "public.report_open"]);
      expect(writing(/DELETE FROM (auth[.]report_holds|public[.]authority_notifications|public[.]productions)/i)).toEqual(["public.erase_authority_records"]);
      // report_close_unsealed has its two callers: the final decision that answered a suspect item, and an unseal_media row.
      expect(writing(/report_close_unsealed[(]/).filter((name) => name !== "public.report_close_unsealed")).toEqual(["public.decisions_apply", "public.report_open"]);
      const fns = ["public.report_open", "public.report_close_unsealed", "public.reports_owed", "public.seal_report", "public.erase_authority_records", "public.authority_records_times", "auth.address_held_until", "auth.address_held", "auth.address_hold_final",
        // 3f's review (0032_orders_review): whether the person was told of every seal behind a held address.
        "auth.address_hold_told"];
      for (const name of fns) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect([f.owner, f.definer, f.config, f.pub], name).toEqual(["korbat_migrate", true, ["search_path=public, pg_temp"], false]);
        expect(f.definition, name).not.toMatch(/interval '/i);
      }
      // seal_report is executable by nobody yet (3d's release will call it), report_close_unsealed by nobody, the auth
      // module's three reads, and the fourth of 3f's review, by korbat_auth alone.
      for (const name of ["public.seal_report", "public.report_close_unsealed", "public.report_open"]) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect([f.api, f.auth], name).toEqual([false, false]);
      }
      for (const name of ["auth.address_held_until", "auth.address_held", "auth.address_hold_final", "auth.address_hold_told"]) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect([f.api, f.auth], name).toEqual([false, true]);
      }
      // The trigger fires after decision_actions_apply, by name, on every insert of a ledger row.
      const [trigger] = await apiDb.execute<{ definition: string }>(sql`select pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid) as definition from pg_trigger t where t.tgname = 'decision_actions_report'`);
      expect(trigger!.definition).toMatch(/AFTER INSERT ON public[.]decision_actions FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION (public[.])?report_open[(][)]/);
      expect("decision_actions_apply" < "decision_actions_report").toBe(true);
    });

    test("3f Task 6's writers (0031_recovery; design, sections 6.6 and 6.7): only gap_close and delete_restore_gaps write a gap, a not-needed closing is held to its audit row at commit, a mark's time is forced, and an imported order's old events pass", async () => {
      const all = await functions();
      const writing = (pattern: RegExp) => all.filter((f) => pattern.test(f.definition)).map((f) => f.name);
      // 3d Task 2 (0034_release; design, section 6.2): the replay of a release closes its gap, as the migrator.
      expect(writing(/(UPDATE|INSERT INTO|DELETE FROM) public[.]restore_gaps/i)).toEqual(["public.delete_restore_gaps", "public.gap_close", "public.release_replay"]);
      expect(writing(/DELETE FROM public[.]copy_marks/i)).toEqual(["public.delete_restore_gaps"]);
      // gap_close is called by the routes alone, never by another function: a decision closes a gap in the API's transaction.
      expect(writing(/gap_close[(]/).filter((name) => name !== "public.gap_close")).toEqual([]);
      for (const name of ["public.gap_close", "public.restore_gaps_confirmed", "public.delete_restore_gaps"]) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect([f.owner, f.definer, f.config, f.pub], name).toEqual(["korbat_migrate", true, ["search_path=public, pg_temp"], false]);
        expect(f.definition, name).not.toMatch(/interval '/i);
      }
      const insert = all.find((found) => found.name === "public.copy_marks_insert")!;
      expect([insert.definer, insert.api, insert.pub]).toEqual([false, false, false]);
      expect(insert.definition).toMatch(/NEW[.]at := clock_timestamp[(][)]/);
      expect([all.find((f) => f.name === "public.restore_gaps_confirmed")!.api, all.find((f) => f.name === "public.gap_close")!.api]).toEqual([false, true]);
      const triggers = await apiDb.execute<{ definition: string }>(
        sql`select pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid) as definition from pg_trigger t where t.tgname in ('restore_gaps_confirmed', 'copy_marks_insert') order by t.tgname`,
      );
      expect(triggers.map((t) => t.definition.replace(/ EXECUTE FUNCTION .*$/, ""))).toEqual([
        "CREATE TRIGGER copy_marks_insert BEFORE INSERT ON public.copy_marks FOR EACH ROW",
        "CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER restore_gaps_confirmed AFTER UPDATE ON public.restore_gaps DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW WHEN (((new.disposition = 'not_needed'::text) AND (old.disposition IS DISTINCT FROM 'not_needed'::text)))",
      ]);
      // legal_order_events_confirmed, replaced from 0028's text, returns for an imported order's event dated before its import.
      expect(all.find((f) => f.name === "public.legal_order_events_confirmed")!.definition).toMatch(/o[.]imported_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW[.]at < o[.]imported_at/);
    });

    test("measures_in_force runs with its reader's rights and names exactly the contracts' measures", async () => {
      const [view] = await apiDb.execute<{ options: string[] | null; definition: string }>(sql`select c.reloptions as options, pg_get_viewdef(c.oid) as definition from pg_class c where c.oid = 'public.measures_in_force'::regclass`);
      expect(view!.options).toEqual(["security_invoker=true"]);
      const measures = ACTION_KINDS.filter((kind) => MEASURES[kind].lifts === null);
      // 3e: the view names its kinds as text (enum-literals.test.ts: a value 3e added cannot be an enum literal in the
      // migration that adds it), and the seal's own literal as the enum; both forms are read.
      const named = [...view!.definition.matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'::(?:action_kind|text)/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
      expect([...new Set(named)].sort()).toEqual([...measures].sort());
      // No value of post_state: a migration that adds one cannot change what "in force" means.
      expect(view!.definition).not.toMatch(/post_state/);
      const columns = await apiDb.execute<{ name: string }>(sql`select attname::text as name from pg_attribute where attrelid = 'public.measures_in_force'::regclass and attnum > 0 order by attnum`);
      expect(columns.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["id", "kind", "post_id", "media_id", "subject_account_id", "decision_id", "decision_kind", "case_id"]);
    });
  });

  describe("each CHECK written from a contracts constant holds exactly that constant's values", () => {
    /** The quoted values of one CHECK, as the migrated database defines it. */
    const checkValues = async (table: string, name: string) => [...(await checkDefinition(table, name)).matchAll(/'([^']*)'/g)].map((m) => m[1]!).sort();
    /** The one number of a length CHECK. */
    async function checkBound(table: string, name: string): Promise<number> {
      const definition = await checkDefinition(table, name);
      const numbers = [...definition.matchAll(/<= (\d+)/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1]));
      expect(numbers, definition).toHaveLength(1);
      return numbers[0]!;
    }

    test("the 16 Transparency Database categories, on intakes and on decisions", async () => {
      expect(await checkValues("intakes", "intakes_category")).toEqual([...TDB_CATEGORIES].sort());
      expect(await checkValues("decisions", "decisions_category")).toEqual([...TDB_CATEGORIES].sort());
    });

    test("the CSAM path's keywords on intakes, and a decision's keywords", async () => {
      const keywords = Object.values(CSAM_KEYWORDS).filter((keyword): keyword is NonNullable<typeof keyword> => keyword !== null);
      expect(await checkValues("intakes", "intakes_category_keyword")).toEqual([...keywords].sort());
      expect(await checkValues("decisions", "decisions_category_keyword")).toEqual([...DECISION_KEYWORDS].sort());
    });

    test("the six rules, on intakes and on decisions", async () => {
      expect(await checkValues("intakes", "intakes_rule_id")).toEqual([...RULE_IDS]);
      expect(await checkValues("decisions", "decisions_rule_id")).toEqual([...RULE_IDS]);
    });

    test("the bounds of a notice's two texts", async () => {
      expect(await checkBound("intakes", "intakes_explanation_len")).toBe(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax);
      expect(await checkBound("intakes", "intakes_cited_law_len")).toBe(NOTICE_LIMITS.citedLawMax);
    });

    test("the ledger's kinds are the contracts' action kinds, in their order, the two of an order's measure last", async () => {
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ label: string }>(sql`select e.enumlabel::text as label from pg_enum e where e.enumtypid = 'public.action_kind'::regtype order by e.enumsortorder`);
      // 3f: the migration orders adds them; they joined ACTION_KINDS with the task that gives effect to an order (Task 3).
      expect(rows.map((row) => row.label)).toEqual([...ACTION_KINDS]);
      expect(ACTION_KINDS.slice(-2)).toEqual([...ORDER_ACTION_KINDS]);
    });

    test("post_state has its four values and 3f's disabled: a seal is a state of images, a disabling one of posts", async () => {
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ label: string }>(sql`select e.enumlabel::text as label from pg_enum e where e.enumtypid = 'public.post_state'::regtype order by e.enumsortorder`);
      expect(rows.map((row) => row.label)).toEqual(["visible", "withheld", "removed", "deleted_by_author", "disabled"]);
    });

    test("no check lets a row through on a null: the database holds the null-safe forms", async () => {
      // A CHECK passes when its expression is null. These five are written so that it never is. PostgreSQL stores
      // "is not distinct from" as the negation of "is distinct from" and prints it that way.
      expect(await checkDefinition("intake_items", "intake_items_case")).toContain("(NOT (outcome IS DISTINCT FROM 'not_available'::item_outcome))");
      expect(await checkDefinition("decisions", "decisions_keyword")).toContain("(NOT (ground IS DISTINCT FROM 'illegal'::decision_ground))");
      expect(await checkDefinition("intake_items", "intake_items_statement")).toContain("statement_digest IS NOT NULL");
      expect(await checkDefinition("appeals", "appeals_statement")).toContain("statement_digest IS NOT NULL");
      expect(await checkDefinition("staff_texts", "staff_texts_digest")).toContain("salt ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'");
    });
  });

  describe("appeal_deadline", () => {
    test("it equals the contracts' appealDeadline on every month end of two years, a leap year among them, and on the days around them", async () => {
      // The last three days of each month of 2027 and 2028 (2028 has a 29 February) and the first of the next, at three times of day.
      // Both times as the text toISOString writes, so that nothing depends on how the driver reads a timestamp.
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ informed: string; deadline: string }>(sql`
        select to_char(t at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as informed, to_char(public.appeal_deadline(t) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as deadline
          from generate_series('2027-01-01'::timestamp, '2028-12-01'::timestamp, interval '1 month') month,
               generate_series(-3, 0) shift,
               unnest(array[interval '0 hours', interval '12 hours 30 minutes 15.25 seconds', interval '23 hours 59 minutes 59.999 seconds']) time_of_day,
               lateral (select (month + interval '1 month' + make_interval(days => shift) + time_of_day) at time zone 'UTC' as t) s
         order by 1`);
      expect(rows).toHaveLength(24 * 4 * 3);
      for (const row of rows) expect(appealDeadline(new Date(row.informed)).toISOString(), row.informed).toBe(row.deadline);
      // The set really holds the clamp: 31 August 2027 is due on the leap day.
      const august = rows.find((row) => row.informed === "2027-08-31T00:00:00.000Z");
      expect(august?.deadline).toBe("2028-02-29T00:00:00.000Z");
    });

    test("it does not depend on the session's time zone", async () => {
      const deadlines = await withLockTimeout(apiDb, async (tx) => {
        const read = async () =>
          (await tx.execute<{ d: string }>(sql`select to_char(public.appeal_deadline('2027-08-30T23:30:00Z'::timestamptz) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as d`))[0]!.d;
        // 30 August, 23:30 UTC, is already the 31st at +14 and still the 30th at -7: a deadline computed in the session's zone
        // would differ between the two, and from UTC's 29 February.
        await tx.execute(sql`set local time zone 'Pacific/Kiritimati'`);
        const east = await read();
        await tx.execute(sql`set local time zone 'America/Los_Angeles'`);
        return [east, await read()];
      });
      expect(deadlines).toEqual(["2028-02-29T23:30:00.000Z", "2028-02-29T23:30:00.000Z"]);
    });
  });

  describe("the forced columns ignore what an insert supplies", () => {
    test("a case starts open, in lane 2, at number 0, whatever the insert said, for the API role and for the migrator", async () => {
      for (const db of [apiDb, migrateDb]) {

            values ('post', ${targetId}::uuid, '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', 0, 7, 7, 9, '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z')
            returning *, (opened_at = now()) as opened_now`);
          expect(row).toMatchObject({ target_type: "post", target_id: targetId, lane: 2, intake_seq: 0, answered_seq: 0, state_version: 0, oldest_open_at: null, last_decided_at: null, closed_at: null, opened_now: true });

            values ('user', ${newRef()}, ${input.lookupHash ?? null}, ${input.channel ?? "signed_in"}::intake_channel, ${input.reporterId ?? null}::uuid, ${input.contactId ?? null}::uuid, ${input.ruleId ?? null},
                    ${input.allegesIllegal ?? false}, ${input.csam ?? false}, ${input.category ?? TC}, ${input.explanation ?? null}, ${input.bonaFide ?? false},
                    '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'sent', '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', null)

        const cases: [string, IntakeInput, string][] = [

          ["a signed-out rule report without a contact", { channel: "signed_out", lookupHash: hex64(), ruleId: "R3" }, "none"],

  describe("the checks of intakes", () => {
    /** One test's intakes, all in a transaction that is rolled back: each insert in a savepoint, its refusal's message or null. */
    const intakes = (fn: (refusal: (input: IntakeInput) => Promise<string | null>, ada: { id: string }) => Promise<void>) =>
      rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
        const ada = await profile(tx);
        await fn(async (input) => (await within(tx, (sp) => insertIntake(sp, input)))?.message ?? null, ada);
      });

    test("a ground is needed: a rule, an allegation of illegality or the CSAM path", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id })).toMatch(/intakes_has_ground/);
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R7" })).toMatch(/intakes_rule_id/);
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R1" })).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("a notice of illegality carries its explanation and its good-faith statement; the CSAM path needs neither", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        const illegal = { reporterId: ada.id, allegesIllegal: true, category: SPEECH };
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_elements/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "why" })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_elements/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, bonaFide: true })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_elements/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "why", bonaFide: true })).toBeNull();
        // A CSAM intake alleges illegality with neither, and with no keyword (the "abuse" choice) or one of the three.
        const csam = { channel: "signed_out" as const, csam: true, allegesIllegal: true, category: MINORS };

      await texts(async (save) => {

        for (const vector of TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS) {
          const salt = hex64();
          const digest = await textDigest(salt, vector.text);
          expect(await save(vector.text, salt, digest), vector.name).toBeNull();
          // The same text under the digest of another salt, or of another text, is refused.
          expect((await save(vector.text, hex64(), digest))?.message, vector.name).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
          expect((await save(`${vector.text}.`, salt, digest))?.message, vector.name).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        }
      });
    });

    test("a digest names one text; a text has a salt; only an erased row has neither", async () => {
      await texts(async (save) => {
        const salt = hex64();
        const digest = await textDigest(salt, "a text");
        expect(await save("a text", salt, digest)).toBeNull();
        expect((await save("a text", salt, digest))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest_unique/);
        expect((await save("a text", null, hex64()))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        expect((await save(null, hex64(), hex64()))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        expect((await save(null, null, hex64()))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        expect((await save("a text", hex64(), hex64(), true))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        // The erased form: text and salt gone, the digest kept.
        expect(await save(null, null, hex64(), true)).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("the salt is 32 bytes as lower-case hex: an empty, a short or an upper-case salt is refused, also with the digest it gives", async () => {
      await texts(async (save, tx) => {
        const salt = hex64();
        // hex decodes either case to the same bytes, so the upper-case spelling has the lower-case salt's digest.
        const upper = salt.toUpperCase();
        expect(await sqlDigest(tx, upper, "a text")).toBe(await textDigest(salt, "a text"));
        for (const malformed of ["", salt.slice(2), upper, `${salt}00`]) {
          const err = await save("a text", malformed, await sqlDigest(tx, malformed, "a text"));
          expect(err, JSON.stringify(malformed)).toMatchObject({ code: "23514", message: expect.stringMatching(/staff_texts_digest/) });
        }
        expect(await save("a text", salt, await textDigest(salt, "a text"))).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("a text longer than 5000 characters is refused whatever its digest", async () => {
      await texts(async (save, tx) => {
        const salt = hex64();
        const long = "x".repeat(5001);
        expect((await save(long, salt, await sqlDigest(tx, salt, long)))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_text_len/);
      });
    });
  });

  test("a decision's keyword needs the ground of the law: on a decision without a ground, or on a rule, it is refused", async () => {
    // The decision is a real one, on a reported post; the migrator then changes its row, the only role that can, in a

    await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {

      const refused = { code: "23514", message: expect.stringMatching(/decisions_keyword/) };

  test("the limits' row is the migration's: 60 decisions an hour and 300 a day, 400 case opens, 50 findings and 10 reveals a day", async () => {
    // The suite's setup leaves this table alone, so the row read here is the one migration 0015 inserted.
    const rows = await apiDb.execute<Record<string, unknown>>(sql`select id, decisions_per_hour, decisions_per_day, case_opens_per_day, findings_per_day, reveals_per_day from moderation_limits`);
    expect(rows.map((row) => ({ ...row }))).toEqual([{ id: 1, decisions_per_hour: 60, decisions_per_day: 300, case_opens_per_day: 400, findings_per_day: 50, reveals_per_day: 10 }]);
    await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {

      expect(err?.message).toMatch(/moderation_limits_single_row/);
    });
  });

  test("this file left no row behind: the tables it writes hold what they held before it", async () => {
    expect(await rowCounts(apiDb)).toEqual(before);
  });
});

 * removal decided, a record to an authority opened and answered, the order verified from the shell, a report answered
 * with no breach. The keeper's file is the tail from 300 places before the backup's head, as a keeper holds it. The

 * another hash and a kept place with another hash are each refused whole; a hole is reported and the run before it
 * imported. The import writes again the order with its original times and its verification, the item's first disabling

 * and one gap for each lost decision and each later step of a record; never a decision or a measure, and the migrator's

    const [record] = await migrateDb.execute<{ state: string; imported: boolean; case_id: string }>(

      ["restriction", "case_decided"],
      ["record", "notification_recorded"],

      ["restriction", "automated_decided"],
      ["no_measure", "case_decided"],
    ]);
    const [program] = await migrateDb.execute<{ target_type: string; target_id: string }>(
      sql`select target_type, target_id from public.restore_gaps where action = 'automated_decided' and place > ${head.seq}`,
    );
    expect({ ...program! }).toEqual({ target_type: "case", target_id: programCase });
    expect(gaps.filter((g) => !g.open).map((g) => g.action).sort()).toEqual(["notification_recorded", "order_opened", "order_recorded"]);
    const [imported] = await migrateDb.execute<{ action: string; counts: Record<string, number> }>(
      sql`select action, metadata -> 'counts' as counts from public.audit_log where chain_seq = (select seq from public.audit_head where id = 1)`,
    );
    expect(imported).toEqual({ action: "restore_imported", counts: { order_effect: 1, restriction: 2, record: 4, no_measure: 1 } });
  });

  test("the migrator's own copy of the lost decision and its measure never commits: decision_holds refuses it without a confirmed audit row", async () => {
    const decisions = await count("decisions");
    // 3f's review (proofs7): the lost answer of no breach needs no texts, so nothing refuses its row at insert and
    // decision_holds at commit is the only guard. (A copy of the lost removal is refused first, for its texts, which the
    // restore lost; the lost order decision for its case, lost with it.)
    const copied = refusal(

            from public.legal_order_items where id = ${itemId}::uuid`,

export function writeRoutes(app: { routes: readonly { method: string; path: string }[] }): string[] {
  const keys = app.routes.filter((route) => !["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "ALL"].includes(route.method) && route.path !== "/api/staff" && !route.path.startsWith("/api/staff/")).map((route) => `${route.method} ${route.path}`);

      "POST /api/media": [{ method: "POST", path: "/api/media", raw: { type: "image/jpeg", body: BYTES.jpeg } }],
      "DELETE /api/media/:id": [{ method: "DELETE", path: `/api/media/${upload.id}` }],
      "POST /api/auth/badge/start": [{ method: "POST", path: "/api/auth/badge/start", json: { phone: `+4477${String(randomInt(10_000_000, 100_000_000))}` } }],
      "POST /api/auth/badge/verify": [{ method: "POST", path: "/api/auth/badge/verify", json: { flowId, code: DEV_CODE } }],
      "POST /api/notices": [
        { method: "POST", path: "/api/notices", json: { ground: "rule", ruleId: "R1", targets: [{ kind: "post", id: bobsPost.id }] } },
        { method: "POST", path: "/api/notices", json: { ground: "illegal", targets: [{ kind: "post", id: bobsPost.id }], category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH", explanation: "It is a threat.", bonaFide: true } },
      ],
      "POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/appeal": [{ method: "POST", path: `/api/moderation/decisions/${decisionId}/appeal`, json: {} }],
      "POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/reply": [{ method: "POST", path: `/api/moderation/decisions/${decisionId}/reply`, json: { statement: "I did not mean it." } }],
      // A person's decision: the request is refused as objection_not_open, never as account_suspended.
      "POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/objection": [{ method: "POST", path: `/api/moderation/decisions/${decisionId}/objection`, json: { text: "Please have a person look at this." } }],
      "POST /api/moderation/items/:item/reexamine": [{ method: "POST", path: `/api/moderation/items/${item!.id}/reexamine`, json: {} }],
    };
    const callsOf = (route: string): Call[] => {
      const given = calls[route];
      if (given) return given;
      // Every other route: called with its path's parameters filled in and an empty body, which is its ordinary answer here.
      const [method, template] = route.split(" ") as [string, string];
      return [{ method, path: template.replace(/:[a-z]+/g, randomUUID()), json: method === "DELETE" ? undefined : {} }];
    };
    const order = writeRoutes(app).sort((a, b) => Number(LAST.includes(a)) - Number(LAST.includes(b)));
    const answers: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const route of order) {
      for (const call of callsOf(route)) {
        const res = await ada.b.fetch(call.path, { method: call.method, json: call.json, raw: call.raw });
        const code = res.status === 403 ? ErrorEnvelope.safeParse(await res.json()).data?.error.code : undefined;
        (answers[route] ??= []).push(code === "account_suspended" ? "refused" : `${res.status}`);
      }
    }
    return { ada, order, answers, state };
  }

  /** Each route answers as section 7.3's table says, and what the refusals left is as it was. */
  async function expectTable({ ada, order, answers }: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof walk>>) {
    for (const route of order) {
      const got = answers[route]!;
      if (route === "POST /api/notices") {
        // A report under a rule is refused; a notice of illegality is taken.
        expect(got, route).toEqual(["refused", "201"]);
        continue;
      }
      if (SUSPENDED_WRITES[route] === "refused") expect(got.every((answer) => answer === "refused"), `${route} answered ${got.join(", ")}`).toBe(true);
      else expect(got.some((answer) => answer === "refused"), `${route} answered ${got.join(", ")}`).toBe(false);
    }
    // What the refusals left: no visible post (its own was deleted; the one the suspension's basis removed is not shown),
    // no follow, the profile and the handle as they were, no badge.
    const [counts] = await apiDb.execute<{ posts: number; follows: number; verified: boolean; handle: string }>(
      sql`select (select count(*)::int from posts where author_id = ${ada.id}::uuid and state = 'visible') as posts,
                 (select count(*)::int from follows where follower_id = ${ada.id}::uuid) as follows,
                 (select verified_at is not null from profiles where id = ${ada.id}::uuid) as verified,
                 (select handle from profiles where id = ${ada.id}::uuid) as handle`,
    );
    expect({ ...counts! }).toEqual({ posts: 0, follows: 0, verified: false, handle: ada.handle });
  }

  test("an account suspended at once: each write route answers 403 account_suspended or its ordinary answer, as the table says, and /api/me then shows the suspension", async () => {
    const result = await walk(async (accountId) => (await suspendForTest(apiDb, accountId, { days: 7 })).decisionId);
    expect(result.state).toBe("running");
    // The reply to a suspension taken at once is late, and taken.
    expect(result.answers["POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/reply"]).toEqual(["201"]);
    // Redress and erasure on real rows of the account's own: its released report examined again, its upload deleted.
    expect(result.answers["POST /api/moderation/items/:item/reexamine"]).toEqual(["201"]);
    expect(result.answers["DELETE /api/media/:id"]).toEqual(["204"]);
    await expectTable(result);
  });

  test("an account terminated at once: the same table, the reply taken, and /api/me shows the termination running", async () => {
    const result = await walk(async (accountId) => (await terminateForTest(apiDb, accountId)).decisionId);
    expect(result.state).toBe("running");
    expect(result.answers["POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/reply"]).toEqual(["201"]);
    expect(result.answers["POST /api/moderation/items/:item/reexamine"]).toEqual(["201"]);
    expect(result.answers["DELETE /api/media/:id"]).toEqual(["204"]);
    await expectTable(result);
  });

  test("an account whose announced suspension has not started: every write route gives its ordinary answer, none refuses it, and its reply comes before the start", async () => {
    const result = await walk(async (accountId) => (await suspendForTest(apiDb, accountId, { announced: true })).decisionId);
    // The decisions of this file are mailed by no auth module: the notice mail's outcome is unknown, so nothing has a start.
    expect(result.state).toBe("unfixed");
    const refused = Object.entries(result.answers).filter(([, got]) => got.includes("refused"));
    expect(refused).toEqual([]);
    expect(result.answers["POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/reply"]).toEqual(["201"]);
    const [reply] = await apiDb.execute<{ on_time: boolean }>(sql`select on_time from suspension_replies where account_id = ${result.ada.id}::uuid`);
    expect(reply?.on_time).toBe(true);
  });

  test("this file left no row behind: what it committed is removed, and the tables hold what they held before it", async () => {
    await closeDecisions();
    await removeFixtures(migrateDb, made.splice(0));
    expect(await rowCounts(apiDb)).toEqual(before);
  });
});

        target_type: "edition",
        target_id: `${YEAR}.1`,
        metadata: { year: YEAR, version: 1, reason: "first" },
        key_id: null,
        step_up: null,
      });
      // Asked again with nothing new: nothing.
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBeNull();

      // In between, more decisions of the year come to light (the spare restrictions move into it), and the held
      // order's hold ends and its notice is told.
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.decisions set decided_at = make_timestamptz(${YEAR}::int, 7, 7, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC') where id = any(${`{${spareIds.join(",")}}`}::uuid[])`);
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = clock_timestamp() where id = ${orders[1]!.id}::uuid`);
      const [told] = await tx.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select public.order_notices_release() as n`);
      expect(told!.n).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBe(2);
      const [, second] = await editions(tx, YEAR);
      expect(second!.reason).toBe("hold_ended");
      const { orders: firstOrders, ...firstTables } = first!.figures;
      const { orders: secondOrders, ...secondTables } = second!.figures;
      expect(secondTables).toEqual(firstTables);
      expect(firstOrders?.received?.total).toBe(1);
      expect(secondOrders?.received).toEqual({ total: 2, crossBorder: 0 });
      expect((await newestAudit(tx)).metadata).toEqual({ year: YEAR, version: 2, reason: "hold_ended" });
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBeNull();

      // A version is never changed, by any role, the migrator included.
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.transparency_editions set figures = '{}'::jsonb where year = ${YEAR} and version = 1`)))).toBe("edition_frozen");
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.transparency_editions set reason = 'correction' where year = ${YEAR} and version = 2`)))).toBe("edition_frozen");

      // The migrator's correction counts every table again, as of the same due day: the spare restrictions now count.
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "correction")).toBe(3);
      const [, , third] = await editions(tx, YEAR);
      expect(third!.reason).toBe("correction");
      expect(third!.figures.restrictions.total).toBe(band(39));
      expect(first!.figures.restrictions.total).toBe(band(24));
      expect(third!.figures.orders?.received).toEqual({ total: 2, crossBorder: 0 });
      // A reason the caller may not give.
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "hold_ended")).toBe("invalid_edition");
    });
  });

  test("the API's role publishes a first version but may not correct one, and may not compute figures itself", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.apiDb, async (tx) => {
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR - 7, "correction")).toBe("invalid_edition");
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR - 7, "hold_ended")).toBe("invalid_edition");
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR - 7, "first")).toBe(1);
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => figuresOf(sp, YEAR - 7)))).toMatch(/^42501/);
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.transparency_editions set reason = 'first' where year = ${YEAR - 7}`)))).toMatch(/^42501/);
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`delete from public.transparency_editions where year = ${YEAR - 7}`)))).toMatch(/^42501/);
    });
  });

  test("the recipients of every version of a year are the six stored months before its due day, whatever the version's instant", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const month = (y: number, m: number) => `${y}-${String(m).padStart(2, "0")}-01`;
      const insert = (y: number, m: number, signedIn: number, signedOutDays: number | null) =>
        tx.execute(sql`insert into public.recipient_months (month, signed_in, signed_out_days, method) values (${month(y, m)}::date, ${signedIn}, ${signedOutDays}, 1)`);
      // September to February: 100 to 150 accounts, 200 to 250 readers summed by day.
      const window: [number, number][] = [[YEAR, 9], [YEAR, 10], [YEAR, 11], [YEAR, 12], [YEAR + 1, 1], [YEAR + 1, 2]];
      for (const [at, [y, m]] of window.entries()) {
        if (at === 5) continue;
        await insert(y, m, 100 + at * 10, 200 + at * 10);
      }
      // Five months: not recorded.
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR)).recipients).toBe("not recorded");
      await insert(YEAR + 1, 2, 150, 250);
      // Months after the due day count for nothing in this edition.
      for (let m = 3; m <= 12; m++) await insert(YEAR + 1, m, 9000, 9000);
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR)).recipients).toEqual({ low: band(125), high: band(125 + 225) });
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBe(1);

      const stored = await editions(tx, YEAR);

      await tx.execute(sql`delete from public.recipient_months where month = ${month(YEAR, 9)}::date`);
      await insert(YEAR, 9, 100, null);
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR)).recipients).toEqual({ low: band(125) });
      // The API's role reads months and inserts one; it updates and deletes none, and computed_at is forced.
      const [row] = await tx.execute<{ fresh: boolean }>(sql`select computed_at = now() as fresh from public.recipient_months where month = ${month(YEAR, 9)}::date`);
      expect(row!.fresh).toBe(true);
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.recipient_months set signed_in = 1 where month = ${month(YEAR, 9)}::date`)))).toBe("edition_frozen");
    });
  });

  test("an order received on 31 December and disabled under a hold on 1 January starts the second version of the year it was received in", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const { orders } = await yearForTest(

        moderator,

      expect(received!.y).toBe(YEAR);

      await tx.execute(sql`select public.order_notices_release()`);

      const [, second] = await editions(tx, YEAR);

      // Received in the year; its one item was disabled in the next, so this year's section counts the order and no item.
      expect(second!.figures.orders?.received).toEqual({ total: 1, crossBorder: 0 });
      expect(second!.figures.orders?.itemsDisabled).toBe(0);
    });
  });

  test("transparency_rules() is TRANSPARENCY_RULES, band over 0 to 200 is the contracts' band, the reasons are EDITION_REASONS, and the grants are 6.4's", async () => {
    const [rules] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ floor: number; round_to: number; due_month: number; due_day: number; method: number }>(sql`select * from public.transparency_rules()`);
    expect({ floor: rules!.floor, roundTo: rules!.round_to, dueMonth: rules!.due_month, dueDay: rules!.due_day, method: rules!.method }).toEqual({ ...TRANSPARENCY_RULES });
    const bands = await w.apiDb.execute<{ n: number; b: string }>(sql`select g::int as n, public.band(g) as b from generate_series(0, 200) g order by g`);
    expect(bands).toHaveLength(201);
    for (const row of bands) expect([row.n, row.b]).toEqual([row.n, band(row.n)]);
    const [check] = await w.migrateDb.execute<{ def: string }>(sql`select pg_get_constraintdef(c.oid) as def from pg_constraint c where c.conrelid = 'public.transparency_editions'::regclass and c.conname = 'transparency_editions_reason'`);
    expect([...check!.def.matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'::text/g)].map((m) => m[1])).toEqual([...EDITION_REASONS]);
    const [rights] = await w.migrateDb.execute<Record<string, boolean>>(sql`
      select has_table_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_editions', 'SELECT') as editions_sel,

             has_table_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_editions', 'UPDATE') as editions_upd,
             has_table_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_editions', 'DELETE') as editions_del,
             has_table_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.recipient_months', 'SELECT') as months_sel,
             has_column_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.recipient_months', 'signed_in', 'INSERT') as months_ins,
             has_column_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.recipient_months', 'computed_at', 'INSERT') as months_time,
             has_table_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.recipient_months', 'UPDATE') as months_upd,
             has_table_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.recipient_months', 'DELETE') as months_del,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_rules()', 'EXECUTE') as rules,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.band(bigint)', 'EXECUTE') as band,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.edition_publish(integer, text)', 'EXECUTE') as publish,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_figures(integer, timestamptz)', 'EXECUTE') as figures,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_orders(integer, timestamptz)', 'EXECUTE') as orders,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_order_ids(integer, timestamptz)', 'EXECUTE') as ids,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_api', 'public.transparency_order_held(uuid, timestamptz)', 'EXECUTE') as held,

    expect({ ...rights }).toEqual({

      editions_del: false,

      months_ins: true,

      publish: true,

/** tco-counts' figures as the order section holds them: without the year and the issuing state. */
function withoutState(counts: TcoCounts): Record<string, unknown> {
  const { year: _year, received, ...rest } = counts;
  return { ...rest, received: received === null ? null : { total: received.total, crossBorder: received.crossBorder } };
}

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY, type OrderView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { hex64, imagePost, newRef, openCase, type TestStaff } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { ageOrderForTest, effectParams, effectWith, orderForTest } from "./orders-fixtures";

/**
 * yearForTest (3d design, section 12; Task 4, grown in Task 6 for decisions without a decider and in Task 7 for refused
 * uploads): a past year of decisions, intakes, appeals, account measures and orders, written cell by cell as the migrator
 * inside the caller's transaction, which the caller rolls back. LAB E wrote its synthetic decisions with the triggers off
 * (`e-counts.sql`); so does this fixture, for the rows of the tables it fills by the hundred: the migrator owns them, and
 * `alter table ... disable trigger user` holds only until the transaction ends, so nothing it writes outlives the test.
 * It does that first, while the transaction has queued no trigger event on those tables, and switches the triggers on
 * again before the orders, which go through 3f's real flows (as cli-counts.test.ts writes its fixture year) and are then
 * moved back into the year by ageOrderForTest.
 *
 * Each row of a cell gets a time in the year (in UTC) spread over its months, as the lab spread them: the row's number
 * modulo 12 picks the month and modulo 28 the day, at noon. A row counted by its later fate (an appeal's answer) has
 * that fate in the year too.
 */

/** A rule's id, or the law: what a restriction cites. */
export type GroundLabel = "R1" | "R2" | "R3" | "R4" | "R5" | "R6" | "law";

/** One order of the year, given effect through 3f's real flows and moved back into the year. */
export interface OrderCell {
  /** How many posts the order names; it disables the first `effectOn` of them (all by default). */
  posts: number;
  effectOn?: number;
  memberState?: "DE" | "FR";
  /** The instant of its last disabling, in the year or after it; noon on 15 June of the year by default. */
  disabledAt?: Date;
  /** Its receipt this many minutes before its last disabling; none recorded when absent. */
  receivedBefore?: number;
  /**
   * A notice held under Section C: its order decisions stay untold, and its hold runs to this instant (written as the
   * hold's recorded end, the one way a past removal order's hold can still run; the test ends it the same way).
   */
  heldUntil?: Date;
}

/** The cells of a year. Every number is how many rows the cell holds. */
export interface YearCells {
  /** Final decisions that restrict, by what they cite, each with one ledger row of `measure` (remove by default). */
  restrictions?: Partial<Record<GroundLabel, number>>;
  measure?: "remove" | "withhold" | "remove_media" | "reset_bio";
  /** Interim decisions that restrict, each citing R4 with one withhold. */
  interim?: number;
  /** Final decisions that found no breach (no_violation). */
  noBreach?: number;
  /** Intakes by kind: a report under a rule, a notice of illegality, a moderator's finding. */
  intakes?: Partial<Record<"rules" | "illegal" | "finding", number>>;
  /** Appeals answered in the year, by their result; each appeals a decision of the year before, so no restriction of the year is added. */
  appeals?: Partial<Record<"kept" | "partly_reversed" | "reversed", number>>;
  /** 3e's account measures, each on a final decision of the year that restricts under R6 (which therefore counts as a restriction too). */
  accountMeasures?: Partial<Record<"strike" | "suspend" | "terminate" | "retire_handle" | "warn_reporting" | "restrict_reporting", number>>;
  orders?: OrderCell[];
  /** Restrictions under R3 dated in the year before, which a test may move into the year later: what a correction counts again. */
  spare?: number;
  /**
   * 3d Task 6: a program's rows. `findings`: intakes of the kind automated on the channel system, by the rule each cites;
   * of the R1 ones, `restrictedR1` have an item on the year's case, so a person's final restriction of the year
   * (`restrictions`, which the test sets) restricted them. `measures`: decisions without a decider, interim, restricting and
   * fully automated, by rule, each with its one ledger row: a withhold of the year's post's image under R1, a seal of its
   * images under R2.
   */
  automated?: { findings?: Partial<Record<"R1" | "R2", number>>; restrictedR1?: number; measures?: Partial<Record<"R1" | "R2", number>> };
}

/** What the fixture made that a test reads again. */
export interface YearMade {
  caseId: string;
  orders: OrderView[];
  /** The decisions of `spare`. */
  spareIds: string[];
}

/** The tables the fixture fills with its triggers off; 3d Task 6 adds the items of a program's findings. */
const BULK_TABLES = ["decisions", "decision_actions", "intakes", "intake_items", "appeals"] as const;

/** A row's time in the year: its number picks the month and the day, at noon UTC. */
const spread = (year: number) => sql`make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 1 + (g::int % 12), 1 + (g::int % 28), 12, 0, 0, 'UTC')`;

export async function yearForTest(tx: DbTx, year: number, cells: YearCells, staff: TestStaff): Promise<YearMade> {
  // One post and its case, which every bulk decision names: the ledger needs a case, a snapshot and a decider.
  // 3d Task 6: with an image when a program's measures withhold one.
  const { authorId, postId, mediaIds } = await imagePost(tx, cells.automated?.measures ? 1 : 0);
  const caseId = await openCase(tx, "post", postId);
  const [snapshot] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
    insert into public.evidence_snapshots (case_id, target_type, target_id, author_handle, digest)
    values (${caseId}::uuid, 'post', ${postId}::uuid, 'author', ${hex64()}) returning id`);
  const spareIds: string[] = [];

  for (const table of BULK_TABLES) await tx.execute(sql.raw(`alter table public.${table} disable trigger user`));
  {
    /** Inserts `n` decisions with the columns given, each with one ledger row of `measure` when it restricts. */
    const decisions = async (n: number, d: { kind: "final" | "interim" | "review"; outcome: string; ground: "incompatible" | "illegal" | null; ruleId: string | null; at: ReturnType<typeof spread>; measure: string | null }) => {
      if (n <= 0) return [] as string[];
      const legal = d.ground === "illegal" ? hex64() : null;
      const restricted = d.outcome === "restricted";
      const rows = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
        insert into public.decisions (case_id, kind, seen_state_version, outcome, ground, rule_id, rules_version, redress_version, category, source,
                                      snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, facts_digest, reason_digest, legal_reference_digest, decided_by, decided_at, xact, puid,
                                      informed_at, suspect, needs_admin, ended_interim)
        select ${caseId}::uuid, ${d.kind}::public.decision_kind, 0, ${d.outcome}::public.decision_outcome, ${d.ground}::public.decision_ground, ${d.ruleId},
               3, 3, 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE', 'report', ${snapshot!.id}::uuid, ${hex64()}, ${restricted ? hex64() : null}, ${restricted ? hex64() : null}, ${legal},
               ${staff.id}::uuid, ${d.at}, '1'::xid8, md5(random()::text || g::text), ${d.at}, false, false, false
          from generate_series(1, ${n}::int) g
        returning id`);
      const ids = rows.map((row) => row.id);
      if (d.measure !== null) {
        await tx.execute(sql`
          insert into public.decision_actions (decision_id, kind, subject_account_id, post_id, created_at)
          select d.id, ${d.measure}::public.action_kind, ${authorId}::uuid, ${postId}::uuid, d.decided_at from public.decisions d where d.id = any(${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[])`);
      }
      return ids;
    };

    const measure = cells.measure ?? "remove";
    for (const [label, n] of Object.entries(cells.restrictions ?? {}) as [GroundLabel, number][]) {

    }

    await decisions(cells.noBreach ?? 0, { kind: "final", outcome: "no_violation", ground: null, ruleId: null, at: spread(year), measure: null });
    spareIds.push(...(await decisions(cells.spare ?? 0, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R3", at: spread(year - 1), measure })));
    for (const [kind, n] of Object.entries(cells.accountMeasures ?? {}) as [string, number][]) {
      await decisions(n, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R6", at: spread(year), measure: kind });
    }

    for (const [label, n] of Object.entries(cells.intakes ?? {}) as ["rules" | "illegal" | "finding", number][]) {
      const finding = label === "finding";
      const illegal = label === "illegal";
      await tx.execute(sql`
        insert into public.intakes (kind, ref, channel, finding_by, rule_id, alleges_illegal, category, explanation, bona_fide, received_at)
        select ${finding ? "finding" : "user"}::public.intake_kind, r.ref,
               ${finding ? "staff" : "signed_in"}::public.intake_channel, ${finding ? staff.id : null}::uuid, ${illegal ? null : finding ? "R3" : "R1"},
               ${illegal}, ${illegal ? "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH" : "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC"}, ${illegal ? "it is illegal" : null}, ${illegal},
               ${spread(year)}
          from unnest(${`{${Array.from({ length: n }, () => newRef()).join(",")}}`}::text[]) with ordinality as r(ref, g)`);
    }

    // 3d Task 6: a program's findings and measures. The new label and channel are cast at run time, on a database that has
    // them; the figures function compares them as text.
    for (const [rule, n] of Object.entries(cells.automated?.findings ?? {}) as ["R1" | "R2", number][]) {
      const restricted = rule === "R1" ? Math.min(n, cells.automated?.restrictedR1 ?? 0) : 0;
      const made = await tx.execute<{ id: string; g: number }>(sql`
        insert into public.intakes (kind, ref, channel, rule_id, alleges_illegal, category, bona_fide, automated_processing, received_at)
        select ${"automated"}::public.intake_kind, r.ref, ${"system"}::public.intake_channel, ${rule}, false, ${RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY[rule]}, false, true, ${spread(year)}
          from unnest(${`{${Array.from({ length: n }, () => newRef()).join(",")}}`}::text[]) with ordinality as r(ref, g)

      for (const [at, intake] of made.slice(0, restricted).entries()) {

                             values (${intake.id}::uuid, 1, 'post', ${postId}::uuid, ${caseId}::uuid, ${100_000 + at}, 2, make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC'))`);
      }
    }
    for (const [rule, n] of Object.entries(cells.automated?.measures ?? {}) as ["R1" | "R2", number][]) {
      const rows = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
        insert into public.decisions (case_id, kind, seen_state_version, outcome, ground, rule_id, rules_version, redress_version, category, source,
                                      snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, decided_by, decided_at, xact, puid, informed_at, suspect, needs_admin, ended_interim,
                                      automated_detection, automated_decision)
        select ${caseId}::uuid, 'interim', 0, 'restricted', 'incompatible', ${rule}, 3, 4, ${RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY[rule]}, 'own_initiative',
               ${snapshot!.id}::uuid, ${hex64()}, null, ${spread(year)}, '1'::xid8, md5(random()::text || g::text), ${spread(year)}, false, false, false, true, 'fully'
          from generate_series(1, ${n}::int) g
        returning id`);
      await tx.execute(sql`
        insert into public.decision_actions (decision_id, kind, media_id, subject_account_id, post_id, created_at)
        select d.id, ${rule === "R1" ? "withhold_media" : "seal_media"}::public.action_kind, ${rule === "R1" ? mediaIds[0]! : null}::uuid, ${authorId}::uuid, ${postId}::uuid, d.decided_at
          from public.decisions d where d.id = any(${`{${rows.map((row) => row.id).join(",")}}`}::uuid[])`);
    }

    // An appeal answered in the year: the decision it appeals is of the year before (so no restriction of the year is
    // added), and the review that answers it is of the year, with the result the cell names.
    for (const [result, n] of Object.entries(cells.appeals ?? {}) as ["kept" | "partly_reversed" | "reversed", number][]) {
      const appealed = await decisions(n, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R1", at: spread(year - 1), measure });
      for (const decisionId of appealed) {
        const [appeal] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
          insert into public.appeals (decision_id, appellant_account_id, filed_at) values (${decisionId}::uuid, ${authorId}::uuid, make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC')) returning id`);
        const [review] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
          insert into public.decisions (case_id, kind, reviews_decision_id, appeal_id, seen_state_version, outcome, rules_version, redress_version, category, source,
                                        snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, reason_digest, decided_by, decided_at, xact, puid, informed_at, suspect, needs_admin, ended_interim)
          values (${caseId}::uuid, 'review', ${decisionId}::uuid, ${appeal!.id}::uuid, 0, ${result}::public.decision_outcome, 3, 3, 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE', 'report',
                  ${snapshot!.id}::uuid, ${hex64()}, ${hex64()}, ${staff.id}::uuid, make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 3, 3, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC'), '1'::xid8, ${randomUUID().replaceAll("-", "")},
                  make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 3, 3, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC'), false, false, false)
          returning id`);
        await tx.execute(sql`update public.appeals set answered_by = ${review!.id}::uuid, result = ${result}::public.appeal_result, answered_at = make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 3, 3, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC')
                              where id = ${appeal!.id}::uuid`);
      }
    }
  }
  // On again for what follows: a failure above aborted the transaction, which the caller rolls back with the switch.
  for (const table of BULK_TABLES) await tx.execute(sql.raw(`alter table public.${table} enable trigger user`));

  const orders: OrderView[] = [];
  for (const cell of cells.orders ?? []) orders.push(await orderOfYear(tx, year, cell, staff));
  return { caseId, orders, spareIds };
}

/**
 * One order of a year, as cli-counts.test.ts's fixture writes one: opened on new posts, its first `effectOn` items given
 * effect, its receipt recorded so many minutes before its last disabling, then every time of it moved back by whole
 * minutes so that its last disabling falls on `disabledAt`. A held one has Section C, so its order decisions are untold,
 * and its hold's recorded end at `heldUntil`.
 */
async function orderOfYear(tx: DbTx, year: number, cell: OrderCell, staff: TestStaff): Promise<OrderView> {
  const posts: string[] = [];
  for (let n = 0; n < cell.posts; n++) posts.push((await imagePost(tx, 1)).postId);
  const order = await orderForTest(tx, staff, { posts, memberState: cell.memberState ?? "DE", sectionC: cell.heldUntil !== undefined });
  const chosen = order.items.slice(0, cell.effectOn ?? order.items.length).map((item) => item.id);
  const view = chosen.length === 0 ? order : await effectWith(tx, staff, order.id, effectParams(order, { itemIds: chosen }));
  if (cell.receivedBefore !== undefined) {
    await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set received_at = coalesce((select max(disabled_at) from public.legal_order_items where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid), opened_at)
                                                                     - make_interval(mins => ${cell.receivedBefore}::int)
                          where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
  }
  const target = cell.disabledAt ?? new Date(Date.UTC(year, 5, 15, 12));
  const [last] = await tx.execute<{ at: string }>(sql`select coalesce(max(disabled_at), (select opened_at from public.legal_orders where id = ${order.id}::uuid))::text as at
                                                       from public.legal_order_items where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
  await ageOrderForTest(tx, order.id, Math.round((new Date(last!.at).getTime() - target.getTime()) / 60_000));
  if (cell.heldUntil !== undefined) {
    await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = ${cell.heldUntil.toISOString()}::timestamptz, hold_end_reason = 'released_by_authority'
                          where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
  }
  return view;
}

 * it meets, measured against the real database with migration 0016. The lab issues the statements itself, as SQL: a
 * decision is its profile lock, its row and its ledger rows, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, a deletion and
 * a purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue. Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the
 * lab leaves no decision. Its one audit row is the R4 removal that the redaction's rounds need committed, which is a real,
 * confirmed decision. The accounts and posts it commits for the two-session rounds and the large accounts are removed at
 * the end. It writes one line of JSON for each measurement, with how busy the machine's
 * processors were just before it. Run it by hand (see README.md); no suite includes it.
 */

/** Where the measurements go, one line of JSON each: the file LAB_OUT names, or lab-contention.jsonl in the repository's .data folder (the lab runs from apps/api). */
const OUT = process.env.LAB_OUT ?? path.resolve(process.cwd(), "../../.data/lab-contention.jsonl");
function line(name: string, result: Record<string, unknown>): void {
  const text = JSON.stringify({ name, at: new Date().toISOString(), ...result });
  mkdirSync(path.dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });
  appendFileSync(OUT, text + String.fromCharCode(10));
  console.log(`LAB ${text}`);
}

/** The share of processor time that was not idle over this many milliseconds, across all cores: how loaded the machine is. */
async function busy(ms = 1500): Promise<number> {
  const read = () => os.cpus().reduce((sum, cpu) => ({ idle: sum.idle + cpu.times.idle, all: sum.all + cpu.times.user + cpu.times.nice + cpu.times.sys + cpu.times.irq + cpu.times.idle }), { idle: 0, all: 0 });
  const before = read();
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
  const after = read();
  return Math.round((1 - (after.idle - before.idle) / Math.max(1, after.all - before.all)) * 100);
}

async function timed(fn: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<number> {
  const start = performance.now();
  await fn();
  return Math.round(performance.now() - start);
}

  test("3f, Task 4: the end of an order's preservation against the ten-item effect of the same order on the same author's posts: forty rounds, both orders", async () => {
    // Migration 0029's order_preservation_end takes the case of the item's decision (and those of the post's other
    // copies), then the item, then the post, then its image rows (design, section 5, the lock order, item 3); the effect
    // transaction takes the authors' profiles, the cases through its intake's items, the items' rows and then, post by
    // post, the snapshot, the decision and the measure. One order of eleven posts by one author: its first item was given
    // effect with a real key and aged past its six months, so every round finds its preservation due again; the other
    // ten are given effect in one transaction with a made-up confirmation of their params. Both sides roll back.
    const started = new Date();
    world ??= deciderWorld(apiDb);
    const staff = await world.staff("moderator");
    const author = await newProfile(apiDb);
    committed.push(author.id);
    const posts: string[] = [];
    for (let n = 0; n < 11; n++) {
      const postId = await newPostRow(apiDb, author.id);
      await newImageRow(apiDb, author.id, postId, 0);
      posts.push(postId);
    }
    const order = await orderForTest(apiDb, staff, { posts });
    const first = order.items[0]!;
    const done = await effectForTest(world, staff, order.id, effectParams(order, { itemIds: [first.id] }));
    if (typeof done === "string") throw new Error(`the lab's first effect was not recorded: ${done}`);
    await ageOrderForTest(migrateDb, order.id, 200 * 24 * 60);
    const ten = done.items.filter((item) => item.id !== first.id).map((item) => item.id);
    const params = effectParams(done, { itemIds: ten });
    const pause = (tx: DbTx) => tx.execute(sql`select pg_sleep(0.015)`);
    const ending = async (tx: DbTx) => {
      const [row] = (await tx.execute(sql`select public.order_preservation_end(${first.id}::uuid) as done`)) as unknown as { done: boolean }[];
      if (!row!.done) throw new Error("the preservation's end changed nothing");
    };
    const effect = async (tx: DbTx) => {
      await effectWith(tx, staff, order.id, params);
    };

    try {
      const ROUNDS = 40;
      const load = await busy();
      line("preservation end alone", { images: 1, busyPercent: load, ms: await timed(() => rolledBack(apiDb, ending)) });
      line("ten-item effect alone", { items: ten.length, busyPercent: load, ms: await timed(() => rolledBack(apiDb, effect)) });
      const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
      let longest = 0;
      for (let round = 0; round < ROUNDS; round++) {
        const side = (fn: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>, delay: number) => async () => {
          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
          const start = performance.now();
          const outcome = await rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
            await fn(tx);
            await pause(tx);
          }).then(
            () => "ok",
            (err: unknown) => {
              const fromDatabase = raised(err);
              return fromDatabase ? `${fromDatabase.code} ${fromDatabase.message}` : ((err as { code?: string }).code ?? String(err));
            },
          );
          longest = Math.max(longest, performance.now() - start);
          return outcome;
        };
        const ahead = Math.floor(Math.random() * 8);
        const [a, b] = await Promise.all(round % 2 === 0 ? [side(ending, 0)(), side(effect, ahead)()] : [side(ending, ahead)(), side(effect, 0)()]);
        for (const [who, outcome] of [["preservation end", a], ["effect", b]] as const) counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] = (counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] ?? 0) + 1;
      }
      line("preservation end contention", { end: "order_preservation_end of one item", against: "the ten-item effect of the same order", rounds: ROUNDS, busyPercent: load, outcomes: counts, longestMs: Math.round(longest) });
    } finally {
      await removeDecided(migrateDb, posts, []);
      await removeOrderAlerts(migrateDb, started);
    }
  });

  test("3f, Task 3: the ten-item effect of one order against an intake on its posts, a seal on one of its authors and the purge of the other: forty rounds each, both orders", async () => {
    // Section 13 asked for this part in Task 3, and 3f's review carried it to Task 8 (ruling 14). The effect transaction
    // (design, section 5, the lock order, items 1 and 2) takes its authors' profiles in id order, the cases through its
    // intake's items, the items' rows and then, post by post, the snapshot, the decision and the measure, whose triggers
    // take the post and its images. Against it: a report and a notice on its posts, which take the cases and the posts'
    // images; an interim seal of one author's images on the path for child sexual abuse material, which takes that
    // author's profile and every image of the account; and the purge of the other author's account, as the repositories
    // issue it. One order of ten posts, five by each author, given effect in one transaction with a made-up confirmation
    // of its params; every side rolls back, so every round finds the order as it was.
    const started = new Date();
    world ??= deciderWorld(apiDb);
    const staff = await world.staff("moderator");
    const [sealed, purged] = [await newProfile(apiDb), await newProfile(apiDb)];
    committed.push(sealed.id, purged.id);

    for (const author of [sealed, purged]) {

    }
