describe("the transparency page's daily value (3d Task 5, 9.3 item 6, W.2)", () => {
  const value = (c: string) => c.repeat(64);
  const head: PublicHead = {
    days: [
      { day: "2026-10-19", kind: "head", value: value("a"), witness: "rfc3161", token: "MAMCAQA=", retiredOn: null, lastDay: null },
      { day: "2026-10-18", kind: "restore", value: value("b"), witness: "none", token: null, retiredOn: null, lastDay: "2026-10-15" },
      { day: "2026-10-17", kind: "head", value: value("c"), witness: "none", token: null, retiredOn: "2026-10-18", lastDay: null },
      { day: "2026-10-15", kind: "head", value: value("d"), witness: "none", token: null, retiredOn: null, lastDay: null },
    ],
  };
  const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;

  test("its section stands after the editions and before the Transparency Database: [tr.head], a row a day newest first with its value and its witness, [tr.restore], [tr.retired] and [tr.headMissing] in their places", () => {
    const text = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} />));
    const at = (part: string) => {
      expect(text, part).toContain(part);
      return text.indexOf(part);
    };
    const order = [
      at(T.none),
      at(T.headHeading),
      at(T.head),
      at(T.headRow("2026-10-19", value("a"), "rfc3161")),
      at(T.restore("2026-10-18", "2026-10-15")),
      at(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-18")),
      at(`${T.headRow("2026-10-17", value("c"), "none")} ${T.retired("2026-10-18")}`),
      at(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-16")),
      at(T.headRow("2026-10-15", value("d"), "none")),
      at(T.tdbHeading),
    ];
    expect([...order].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(order);
    // A restore that found nothing that still fits says so; a day after the newest row is not shown as missing.
    expect(T.restore("2026-10-18", null)).toBe("2026-10-18: korbat restored its database from a backup. No value above still fits the restored log.");
    expect(text).not.toContain(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-20"));
    expect(text).not.toContain(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-14"));
    // A public page points at no person, and the head's place is in no row.
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/@|chainSeq|chain_seq|Place:/);
  });

  test("while a shown row has a proof: [tr.verify] as the lab ran it, with that day's value and file, and the proof to download as <day>.tsr; without one, neither", () => {
    const markup = html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} />);
    const text = textOf(markup);
    expect(text).toContain(T.verify(value("a"), "2026-10-19"));
    expect(T.verify(value("a"), "2026-10-19")).toBe(
      `To check a day: download its proof, get the timestamp authority's certificates from the authority itself, and run: openssl ts -verify -digest ${value("a")} -in 2026-10-19.tsr -CAfile <certificates>. It answers "Verification: OK" when that authority signed this value at the time the proof states.`,
    );
    expect(text).toContain(T.download("2026-10-19"));
    // One row has a proof, so one download: the words before the day are the same for every row.
    expect(text.split(T.download("DAY").split("DAY")[0]!).length - 1).toBe(1);
    const unwitnessed: PublicHead = { days: head.days.map((row) => ({ ...row, witness: "none", token: null })) };
    const plain = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={unwitnessed} />));
    expect(plain).not.toContain("openssl");
    expect(plain).not.toContain(T.download("2026-10-19"));
    expect(plain).toContain(T.headRow("2026-10-19", value("a"), "none"));
  });

  test("[page.down] for this part alone; no value yet reads its sentence; while it loads, the section holds [tr.head] alone", () => {
    const down = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head="down" />));
    expect(down).toContain(T.none);
    expect(down.split(PAGE_DOWN).length - 1).toBe(1);
    expect(down.indexOf(PAGE_DOWN)).toBeGreaterThan(down.indexOf(T.head));
    const both = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer="down" head="down" />));
    expect(both.split(PAGE_DOWN).length - 1).toBe(2);
    expect(textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={{ days: [] }} />))).toContain(T.headNone);
    const loading = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head="loading" />));
    expect(loading).toContain(T.head);
    expect(loading).not.toContain(PAGE_DOWN);
    expect(loading).not.toContain(T.headNone);
  });

  test("its words are W.2's: [tr.head], [tr.headMissing], [tr.restore] and [tr.retired]", () => {
    expect(T.head).toBe(
      "Each day korbat publishes one value computed from the day and the newest entry of its staff audit log, the record of everything korbat's staff confirm with their keys. If an earlier entry were changed or removed later, the log would no longer lead to the values published since. A value shows neither how many entries the log has nor any entry, and it differs from one day to the next also when nothing was added to the log. A value on korbat's own page proves nothing against korbat's operator, who could change this page too: so the same value goes each day to a person who does not run the server, and, when the outside timestamp is on, to a timestamp authority.",
    );
    expect(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-16")).toBe("2026-10-16: no value was published");
    expect(T.restore("2026-10-18", "2026-10-15")).toBe("2026-10-18: korbat restored its database from a backup. The newest value above that still fits the restored log is of 2026-10-15.");
    expect(T.retired("2026-10-18")).toBe("retired by the restore of 2026-10-18: true when published, and fits no log now");
  });
});

import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { loadConfig } from "../src/config";

const base = { MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: "/media/uploads", MEDIA_STORE_DIR: "/media/store" };

describe("worker configuration", () => {
  test("two directories are all it needs; every format is enabled by default", () => {
    expect(loadConfig(base)).toEqual({
      production: false,
      logLevel: "info",
      uploadsDir: "/media/uploads",
      storeDir: "/media/store",
      formats: ["jpeg", "png", "webp", "gif", "avif"],
      r1Classifier: "off",
    });
  });

  test("3d Task 6: the R1 scorer is off unless set; test only on a closed site; onnx is no adapter of this build", () => {
    expect(loadConfig({ ...base, R1_CLASSIFIER: "" }).r1Classifier).toBe("off");
    expect(loadConfig({ ...base, R1_CLASSIFIER: "test", APP_SITE: "closed" }).r1Classifier).toBe("test");
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, R1_CLASSIFIER: "test" })).toThrow(/R1_CLASSIFIER=test is refused while APP_SITE is open/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, R1_CLASSIFIER: "test", APP_SITE: "open" })).toThrow(/R1_CLASSIFIER=test is refused while APP_SITE is open/);
    // In production too: the refusal holds in every environment.
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, NODE_ENV: "production", VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED: "1", R1_CLASSIFIER: "test" })).toThrow(/APP_SITE is open/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, R1_CLASSIFIER: "onnx", APP_SITE: "closed" })).toThrow(/no such adapter in this build/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, R1_CLASSIFIER: "clip" })).toThrow(/R1_CLASSIFIER/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, APP_SITE: "ajar" })).toThrow(/APP_SITE/);
  });

  test("MEDIA_FORMATS enables a subset, and a typo stops the process", () => {
    expect(loadConfig({ ...base, MEDIA_FORMATS: "jpeg,png" }).formats).toEqual(["jpeg", "png"]);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, MEDIA_FORMATS: "jpeg,heic" })).toThrow(/unknown formats: heic/);
  });

  test("a missing directory is named", () => {
    expect(() => loadConfig({ MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: "/media/uploads" })).toThrow(/MEDIA_STORE_DIR/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ MEDIA_STORE_DIR: "/media/store" })).toThrow(/MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR/);
  });

  test("production refuses to start unless libvips was told to block untrusted loaders", () => {
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...base, NODE_ENV: "production" })).toThrow(/VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED/);
    expect(loadConfig({ ...base, NODE_ENV: "production", VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED: "1" }).production).toBe(true);
  });
});

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

/** Two fresh volumes and a loop around a stand-in pipeline, so these tests are about the protocol only. */
async function harness(process: LoopDeps["process"] = async () => READY) {
  const root = path.join(ws.dir, randomUUID());
  const uploads = uploadsLayout(path.join(root, "uploads"));
  const store = storeLayout(path.join(root, "store"));
  for (const dir of [uploads.tmp, uploads.incoming, uploads.deletions]) mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  await prepareStore(store);
  const calls: string[] = [];
  const aborted: string[] = [];
  let clock = 1_800_000_000_000;
  const deps: LoopDeps = {
    uploads,
    store,
    formats: MEDIA_FORMATS,
    log: pino({ level: "silent" }),
    now: () => (clock += 5),
    process: async (file, formats) => {
      calls.push(path.basename(file));
      return process(file, formats);
    },
    abort: (reason) => void aborted.push(reason),
    watchdogMs: 10_000,
  };
  const upload = (data: Buffer | string = "bytes", id: string = randomUUID()) => {
    writeFileSync(uploads.upload(id), data);
    return id;
  };
  const result = (id: string) => ResultFile.parse(JSON.parse(readFileSync(store.result(id), "utf8")));
  return { deps, uploads, store, upload, result, calls, aborted };
}

    expect(readFileSync(h.store.image(id, "large"), "utf8")).toBe("large-bytes");
    expect(readFileSync(h.store.image(id, "small"), "utf8")).toBe("small-bytes");
    expect(readFileSync(h.store.attempt(id), "utf8")).toBe("1");

  });

  test("3d Task 6: with a scorer's answer, the ready result carries its model and score, and the log line holds neither", async () => {
    const h = await harness(async () => ({ ...READY, r1: { model: "korbat-test-marker", score: 1 } }));
    const id = h.upload();
    await tick(h.deps);
    expect(h.result(id)).toEqual({ v: 2, id, status: "ready", width: 800, height: 600, blurhash: "L2Eo_P_3jb_3", r1: { model: "korbat-test-marker", score: 1 } });
  });

  test("a refused upload gets a failed result with the reason and no files", async () => {

    h.deps.watchdogMs = 30;

import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import sharp from "sharp";
import { MEDIA_FORMATS, R1_MARKER, R1_TEST_MODEL } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { configureDecoder, processImage, type Processed } from "../src/pipeline";
import { testScorer } from "../src/score";
import * as make from "./fixtures";

const ws = make.workspace();
const run = async (name: string, data: Buffer): Promise<Processed> => processImage(ws.file(name, data), MEDIA_FORMATS);
const ready = (result: Processed) => {
  if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`expected a processed image, got ${result.reason}`);
  return result;
};

beforeAll(() => configureDecoder(MEDIA_FORMATS));
afterAll(() => ws.remove());

describe("the decoder allowlist", () => {
  test("every enabled format decodes, so no loader class name is misspelled", async () => {
    for (const [name, data] of Object.entries({ jpeg: await make.jpeg(), png: await make.png(), webp: await make.webp(), gif: await make.gif(), avif: await make.avif() })) {
      expect((await sharp(data).metadata()).width, name).toBe(400);
    }
  });

  test("the decoder itself refuses SVG and TIFF, which the prebuilt binary could otherwise read", async () => {
    await expect(sharp(make.svg()).metadata()).rejects.toThrow(/unsupported image format/);

describe("accepted images", () => {
  test.each(["jpeg", "png", "webp", "gif", "avif"] as const)("%s becomes two WebP files and a blurhash, never enlarged", async (format) => {
    const result = ready(await run(`in.${format}`, await make[format]()));
    expect([result.width, result.height]).toEqual([400, 200]);
    expect(result.blurhash).toMatch(/^[0-9A-Za-z#$%*+,\-.:;=?@[\]^_{|}~]{6,}$/);
    for (const data of [result.large, result.small]) {
      expect(data.subarray(0, 4).toString("latin1")).toBe("RIFF");
      expect(data.subarray(8, 12).toString("latin1")).toBe("WEBP");
      expect(await sharp(data).metadata()).toMatchObject({ format: "webp", width: 400, height: 200 });
    }
  });

    const result = ready(await run("big.jpg", await make.jpeg(3000, 1500)));

    expect(await sharp(result.large).metadata()).toMatchObject({ width: 2048, height: 1024 });
    expect(await sharp(result.small).metadata()).toMatchObject({ width: 1024, height: 512 });
  });

  test("transparency survives", async () => {
    const result = ready(await run("alpha.png", await make.png()));
    expect((await sharp(result.large).metadata()).hasAlpha).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the EXIF rotation is applied, and nothing of the original's metadata survives", async () => {
    const original = await make.photoWithMetadata();
    const before = await sharp(original).metadata();
    expect(before.orientation).toBe(6);
    expect(original.includes(make.SECRET)).toBe(true);
    expect(before.icc).toBeDefined();

    const result = ready(await run("sideways.jpg", original));
    expect([result.width, result.height]).toEqual([200, 400]);
    for (const data of [result.large, result.small]) {
      const meta = await sharp(data).metadata();
      expect([meta.exif, meta.icc, meta.xmp, meta.iptc, meta.orientation]).toEqual([undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined]);
      expect(data.includes(make.SECRET)).toBe(false);
      expect(data.includes("GPS")).toBe(false);
    }
  });

    const result = ready(await run("polyglot.jpg", Buffer.concat([await make.jpeg(), Buffer.from(marker, "latin1")])));
    expect(result.large.includes("hidden-archive-payload")).toBe(false);
    expect(result.small.includes("hidden-archive-payload")).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("3d Task 6: the R1 scorer through the real pipeline (design, sections 5 and 12)", () => {
  /** An image of the given format, of one colour, with or without the marker's block in its top left corner. */
  async function withMarker(format: "png" | "jpeg" | "webp", width: number, height: number, marked: boolean): Promise<Buffer> {
    const base = sharp({ create: { width, height, channels: 3, background: { r: 30, g: 120, b: 60 } } });
    const block = await sharp({ create: { width: R1_MARKER.side, height: R1_MARKER.side, channels: 3, background: { r: R1_MARKER.red, g: R1_MARKER.green, b: R1_MARKER.blue } } }).png().toBuffer();
    const image = marked ? base.composite([{ input: block, left: 0, top: 0 }]) : base;
    return format === "png" ? image.png().toBuffer() : format === "jpeg" ? image.jpeg({ quality: 90 }).toBuffer() : image.webp({ quality: 90 }).toBuffer();
  }

  test("the marker survives the decode, the resize to the small size and the conversion to sRGB, as PNG, JPEG and WebP", async () => {
    for (const format of ["png", "jpeg", "webp"] as const) {
      // 1600 pixels wide: the small size halves it, so the marker's block reaches the scorer at half its side.
      const marked = ready(await processImage(ws.file(`marked.${format}`, await withMarker(format, 1600, 900, true)), MEDIA_FORMATS, testScorer));
      expect(marked.r1, format).toEqual({ model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 1 });
      const plain = ready(await processImage(ws.file(`plain.${format}`, await withMarker(format, 1600, 900, false)), MEDIA_FORMATS, testScorer));
      expect(plain.r1, format).toEqual({ model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 0 });
    }
  });

  test("without a scorer nothing is scored: the result carries no r1", async () => {
    const result = ready(await processImage(ws.file("unscored.png", await withMarker("png", 400, 300, true)), MEDIA_FORMATS));
    expect(result.r1).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test("a scorer is handed the small size's raw pixels and their shape, and nothing else", async () => {
    const seen: { length: number; width: number; height: number; channels: number }[] = [];
    const recording = { model: "recording", score: async (pixels: Uint8Array, width: number, height: number, channels: number) => (seen.push({ length: pixels.length, width, height, channels }), 0.25) };
    const result = ready(await processImage(ws.file("seen.png", await withMarker("png", 1600, 900, false)), MEDIA_FORMATS, recording));
    expect(result.r1).toEqual({ model: "recording", score: 0.25 });
    expect(seen).toEqual([{ length: 1024 * 576 * 3, width: 1024, height: 576, channels: 3 }]);
  });
});

import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_KINDS, ALERT_KIND_LIST, HEAD_KINDS, HEAD_RULES, HEAD_WITNESSES, PublicHead, SENTENCE_MAIL_KINDS, alertPlaceholders, isTimeFact, renderAlert } from "../src/index";

/**
 * 3d Task 5, the audit head's daily value (design, sections 7.7, 10.1, 10.6 and 18, W.7): the head's constants, the two
 * closed lists of head_publications, the public answer, which never holds the place, and the two alerts the
 * transparency job writes, whose one fact is a day.
 */
describe("the head's contracts (3d Task 5)", () => {
  test("HEAD_RULES: the digest's tag, thirty days shown, the witness bounded at ten seconds, a token of at most 16 KB", () => {
    expect({ ...HEAD_RULES }).toEqual({ tag: "korbat.head.v2", shownDays: 30, witnessTimeoutMs: 10_000, tokenMaxBytes: 16_384 });
    expect([...HEAD_KINDS]).toEqual(["head", "restore"]);
    expect([...HEAD_WITNESSES]).toEqual(["none", "rfc3161", "test"]);
  });

  const VALUE = "917907fc36f065a78e0b730230eac9c4f1c2882c77efc7a868a65ee336e0899e";
  const row = { day: "2026-10-18", kind: "head", value: VALUE, witness: "rfc3161", token: "MAMCAQA=", retiredOn: null, lastDay: null } as const;

  test("PublicHead: a day, its kind, its value, who witnessed it with the token, when a restore retired it and, on a restore, the last day that still fits", () => {
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [row] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, witness: "none", token: null }, { ...row, kind: "restore", lastDay: "2026-10-12", retiredOn: null }] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, retiredOn: "2026-10-19" }] }).success).toBe(true);
    // Never the place, the hash or anything a row does not have.
    for (const extra of [{ chainSeq: 41 }, { seq: 41 }, { hash: VALUE }, { publishedAt: "2026-10-18T07:01:00.000Z" }]) {
      expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, ...extra }] }).success, Object.keys(extra)[0]).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const bad of [{ value: VALUE.toUpperCase() }, { value: VALUE.slice(1) }, { witness: "tsa" }, { kind: "retired" }, { day: "18.10.2026" }, { token: "not base64!" }]) {
      expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, ...bad }] }).success, JSON.stringify(bad)).toBe(false);
    }
    // A token is at most HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes bytes, as base64: four characters for each three bytes.
    const groups = Math.ceil(HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes / 3);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, token: `${"A".repeat(groups * 4 - 4)}AA==` }] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, token: "A".repeat(groups * 4 + 4) }] }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("head_unwitnessed and head_missed (W.7): the transparency job's two alerts, a day each", () => {
  const now = new Date("2026-10-18T09:00:00.000Z");

  test("they follow edge_purge_failed in the list, a push and a sentence to every staff account, with the one fact day", () => {
    // 3d Task 6's three kinds follow them (automation.test.ts).
    expect(ALERT_KIND_LIST.slice(-6, -3)).toEqual(["edge_purge_failed", "head_unwitnessed", "head_missed"]);
    for (const kind of ["head_unwitnessed", "head_missed"] as const) {
      expect(ALERT_KINDS[kind], kind).toEqual({ priority: 3, scope: "all", legs: ["push", "mail"], mail: "sentence", facts: ["day"] });
      expect(SENTENCE_MAIL_KINDS, kind).toContain(kind);
      expect(alertPlaceholders(kind), kind).toEqual(["day"]);
    }
    // The day is the day's first instant in the row (alert_outbox's facts hold counts and instants), so it is a time fact.
    expect(isTimeFact("day")).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the day prints as a date, whether it is today's or an earlier one, never as a time of day", () => {
    expect(renderAlert("head_unwitnessed", { day: "2026-10-18T00:00:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "A daily value has no outside timestamp",
      sentence: "The audit log's value of 2026-10-18 was published without an outside timestamp: the timestamp authority did not answer.",
      todo: "Nothing to do for one day. If it repeats, the operator checks the authority's address.",
    });
    expect(renderAlert("head_missed", { day: "2026-10-17T00:00:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "No daily value was published",
      sentence: "No value of the audit log was published for 2026-10-17.",
      todo: "The operator checks that the API ran at the dispatch hour. The keeper notes the gap; the page shows it.",
    });
    // Two sets of facts differ in their digits alone.
    const a = renderAlert("head_missed", { day: "2026-10-13T00:00:00.000Z" }, now).sentence;
    const b = renderAlert("head_missed", { day: "2025-01-02T00:00:00.000Z" }, now).sentence;
    expect(a).not.toBe(b);
    expect(a.replace(/[0-9]/g, "")).toBe(b.replace(/[0-9]/g, ""));
  });

  test("a day that is no instant, or a count in its place, is refused: an alert never goes out with a hole", () => {
    expect(() => renderAlert("head_missed", { day: "2026-10-17" }, now)).toThrow(/day/);
    expect(() => renderAlert("head_missed", { day: 17 }, now)).toThrow(/day/);
    expect(() => renderAlert("head_unwitnessed", {}, now)).toThrow(/day/);
  });
});

describe("laneFor", () => {
  const TC: TdbCategory = "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC";

  test("a rule report takes its rule's lane: R2 and R5 are urgent, R3 and R4 next, R1 and R6 last", () => {
    const lanes = RULE_IDS.map((ruleId) => laneFor({ ruleId, allegesIllegal: false, csam: false, category: TC }));
    expect(lanes).toEqual([2, 0, 1, 1, 0, 2]);
  });

  test("the CSAM path is lane 0 whatever else the intake says", () => {
    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: null, allegesIllegal: true, csam: true, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS" })).toBe(0);
    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: null, allegesIllegal: false, csam: true, category: TC })).toBe(0);
  });

  test("a notice of illegality takes its category's lane, for every category", () => {
    const urgent = ["STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE", "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY", "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM"];
    const next = [
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
    ];
    for (const category of TDB_CATEGORIES) {
      const expected = urgent.includes(category) ? 0 : next.includes(category) ? 1 : 2;
      expect(laneFor({ ruleId: null, allegesIllegal: true, csam: false, category }), category).toBe(expected);
    }
  });

  test("a notice of illegality that also cites a rule takes the more severe of the two lanes", () => {
    // Fraud (lane 2) under R5 (lane 0), and violence (lane 0) under R1 (lane 2): both are urgent.
    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: "R5", allegesIllegal: true, csam: false, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD" })).toBe(0);
    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: "R1", allegesIllegal: true, csam: false, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE" })).toBe(0);
    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: "R3", allegesIllegal: true, csam: false, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD" })).toBe(1);
    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: "R6", allegesIllegal: true, csam: false, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE" })).toBe(2);
  });

  test("where nothing is alleged to be illegal, the category is korbat's own classification and moves no lane", () => {
    for (const category of TDB_CATEGORIES) {
      expect(laneFor({ ruleId: "R1", allegesIllegal: false, csam: false, category }), category).toBe(2);
      expect(laneFor({ ruleId: "R3", allegesIllegal: false, csam: false, category }), category).toBe(1);
    }
  });
});

describe("limits and periods", () => {
  test("the notice limits: per network signed out, per account signed in, ten targets, and the two text bounds", () => {
    expect(NOTICE_LIMITS).toEqual({ signedOut: { perHour: 5, perDay: 20 }, signedIn: { perHour: 10, perDay: 50 }, maxTargets: 10, explanationMax: 2000, citedLawMax: 300 });
  });

  test("a notice on the CSAM path names at most one account; a seal's list shows 500 rows; earlier answers count for 12 months", () => {
    expect(CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS).toBe(1);
    expect(SEAL_LIST_MAX).toBe(500);
    expect(SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS).toBe(12);
  });

  test("six months to appeal or to ask for a re-examination, five of each a day", () => {
    expect(APPEAL_MONTHS).toBe(6);
    expect(DAILY_LIMITS).toEqual({ appeals: 5, reexaminations: 5 });
  });

  test("the retention periods of the design's table", () => {
    expect(RETENTION).toEqual({
      r4FinalMonths: 6,
      intakeDays: 30,
      resetValueDays: 30,
      evidenceHours: 24,
      statementMonths: 12,
      accessLogMonths: 12,
      contactMonths: 6,
      contactMaxMonths: 13,
      confirmationDays: 30,
      backupDays: 30,
      draftHours: 24,
      mailGiveUpDays: 5,
      // 3e (design, sections 6.7 and 10.1, W.7): a reply's text, the reporting counts and the record of standing measures.
      replyText: "until korbat has answered it and its decision can no longer be appealed",
      reportCountDays: 90,
      standingRecord: { strikeDays: 90, ladderMemoryDays: 365, warningDays: 90 },
      // 3f (design, sections 6.8 and 10.1, W.6): a handled message, what a removal order disabled, an order's and an
      // authority's records, and a restore gap closed as not needed or imported.
      contactMessageDays: 30,
      orderPreserveMonths: 6,
      orderRecordYears: 3,
      restoreGapMonths: 12,
    });
    // Content restricted under R4 goes when its restriction is final: the appeal's window.
    expect(RETENTION.r4FinalMonths).toBe(APPEAL_MONTHS);
    // 3e's periods are the standing rules' own numbers, read from STANDING_RULES and never typed twice.
    expect(RETENTION.reportCountDays).toBe(STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays);
    expect(RETENTION.standingRecord).toEqual({ strikeDays: STANDING_RULES.strikeDays, ladderMemoryDays: STANDING_RULES.ladderMemoryDays, warningDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays });
    // 3f's are order_rules()' own numbers, read from ORDER_RULES, which mirrors the function, and never typed twice.
    expect([RETENTION.contactMessageDays, RETENTION.orderPreserveMonths, RETENTION.orderRecordYears, RETENTION.restoreGapMonths]).toEqual([
      ORDER_RULES.messageKeepDays,
      ORDER_RULES.preserveMonths,
      ORDER_RULES.recordKeepYears,
      ORDER_RULES.gapKeepMonths,
    ]);
  });
});

describe("the measures", () => {
  const kinds = Object.keys(MEASURES) as ActionKind[];
  const measures = kinds.filter((kind) => MEASURES[kind].lifts === null);
  const reversals = kinds.filter((kind) => MEASURES[kind].lifts !== null);

  test("every action kind has an entry: 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six measures and four reversals, then 3f's measure and its reversal", () => {
    expect(kinds).toEqual([
      "withhold",
      "remove",
      "seal_media",
      "withhold_media",
      "remove_media",
      "reset_display_name",
      "reset_bio",
      "restore",
      "unseal_media",
      "restore_media",
      "restore_display_name",
      "restore_bio",
      "strike",
      "suspend",
      "terminate",
      "retire_handle",
      "warn_reporting",
      "restrict_reporting",
      "overrule",
      "lift_suspension",
      "unretire_handle",
      "lift_reporting",
      "disable_by_order",
      "reinstate_by_order",
    ]);
    expect(ACTION_KINDS).toEqual(kinds);
    expect(ACTION_KINDS).toHaveLength(24);
    expect(measures).toEqual([...kinds.slice(0, 7), ...kinds.slice(12, 18), "disable_by_order"]);
    expect(reversals).toEqual([...kinds.slice(7, 12), ...kinds.slice(18, 22), "reinstate_by_order"]);
    expect(MEASURE_KINDS).toEqual(measures);
    expect(MEASURE_KINDS).toHaveLength(14);
    expect(REVERSAL_KINDS).toEqual(reversals);
    expect(REVERSAL_KINDS).toHaveLength(10);
  });

  test("a post or one image is withheld only while deciding and removed only when the case is decided; a seal and a reset are either; 3e's measures only when it is decided", () => {
    const when = (kind: ActionKind) => [MEASURES[kind].interim, MEASURES[kind].final];
    expect(when("withhold")).toEqual([true, false]);
    expect(when("withhold_media")).toEqual([true, false]);
    expect(when("remove")).toEqual([false, true]);
    expect(when("remove_media")).toEqual([false, true]);
    for (const kind of ["seal_media", "reset_display_name", "reset_bio"] as const) expect(when(kind), kind).toEqual([true, true]);
    for (const kind of ["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"] as const) expect(when(kind), kind).toEqual([false, true]);
    // A reversal is neither: which decision may hold one is the reversed measure's matter.
    for (const kind of reversals) expect(when(kind), kind).toEqual([false, false]);
  });

  test("each measure has its target, and each reversal lifts the measures of its own target", () => {
    expect(Object.fromEntries(kinds.map((kind) => [kind, MEASURES[kind].target]))).toEqual({
      withhold: "post",
      remove: "post",
      seal_media: "images",
      withhold_media: "image",
      remove_media: "image",
      reset_display_name: "display_name",
      reset_bio: "bio",
      restore: "post",
      unseal_media: "images",
      restore_media: "image",
      restore_display_name: "display_name",
      restore_bio: "bio",
      strike: "account",
      suspend: "account",
      terminate: "account",
      retire_handle: "handle",
      warn_reporting: "reporting",
      restrict_reporting: "reporting",
      overrule: "account",
      lift_suspension: "account",
      unretire_handle: "handle",
      lift_reporting: "reporting",
      disable_by_order: "post",
      reinstate_by_order: "post",
    });
    expect(Object.fromEntries(reversals.map((kind) => [kind, MEASURES[kind].lifts]))).toEqual({
      restore: ["withhold", "remove"],
      unseal_media: ["seal_media"],
      restore_media: ["withhold_media", "remove_media"],
      restore_display_name: ["reset_display_name"],
      restore_bio: ["reset_bio"],
      overrule: ["strike"],
      lift_suspension: ["suspend", "terminate"],
      unretire_handle: ["retire_handle"],
      lift_reporting: ["warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"],
      reinstate_by_order: ["disable_by_order"],
    });
    // Every measure can be lifted, by exactly one kind of reversal, of the measure's own target.
    for (const measure of measures) expect(reversals.filter((kind) => (MEASURES[kind].lifts as readonly ActionKind[]).includes(measure)), measure).toHaveLength(1);
    for (const kind of reversals) for (const lifted of MEASURES[kind].lifts as readonly ActionKind[]) expect(MEASURES[lifted].target, kind).toBe(MEASURES[kind].target);
    // Only the three timed kinds sign their days and whether they are announced.
    expect(TIMED_KINDS).toEqual(["suspend", "terminate", "restrict_reporting"]);
  });

  test("each has a label of its own: the composer's words where the composer names the measure", () => {
    // The first seven and "Lift the seal" are the words of the decision composer; the composer, the statement and the
    // terms all take them from here. 3e's are W.1's.
    expect(Object.fromEntries(kinds.map((kind) => [kind, MEASURES[kind].label]))).toEqual({
      withhold: "Withhold the post",
      remove: "Remove",
      seal_media: "Seal the images this case reaches",
      withhold_media: "Withhold one image",
      remove_media: "Remove one image",
      reset_display_name: "Reset display name",
      reset_bio: "Reset bio",
      restore: "Lift the restriction of the post",
      unseal_media: "Lift the seal",
      restore_media: "Lift the restriction of one image",
      restore_display_name: "Lift the reset of the display name",
      restore_bio: "Lift the reset of the bio",
      strike: "Strike",
      suspend: "Suspend the account",
      terminate: "Terminate the account",
      retire_handle: "Retire the handle",
      warn_reporting: "Warn about reporting",
      restrict_reporting: "Restrict reporting",
      overrule: "Overrule the strike",
      lift_suspension: "Lift the suspension",
      unretire_handle: "Give the handle back",
      lift_reporting: "Lift the reporting measure",
      // 3f (W.1).
      disable_by_order: "Disabled for an order",
      reinstate_by_order: "Reinstate after an order",
    });
    const labels = kinds.map((kind) => MEASURES[kind].label);
    expect(new Set(labels).size).toBe(labels.length);
  });
});

describe("the order of a decision's actions", () => {
  const a = "1a1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
  const b = "2a1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";

  test("by kind as a string, then by image as a string, an action without an image first", () => {
    const sorted: DecisionActionParams[] = [
      { kind: "remove", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: a },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: b },
      { kind: "reset_bio", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "seal_media", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: a },
    ];
    for (const shuffled of [[...sorted].reverse(), [sorted[3]!, sorted[0]!, sorted[5]!, sorted[2]!, sorted[1]!, sorted[4]!]]) {
      expect([...shuffled].sort(compareDecisionActions)).toEqual(sorted);
    }
    expect(compareDecisionActions(sorted[1]!, sorted[1]!)).toBe(0);
    expect(compareDecisionActions({ kind: "restore_media", mediaId: null }, { kind: "restore_media", mediaId: a })).toBeLessThan(0);
  });
});

describe("textDigest", () => {
  test("the tag names the version of the rule", () => {
    expect(TEXT_DIGEST_TAG).toBe("korbat.text.v1");
  });

  test.each(TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => [vector.name, vector] as const))("%s: the sha256 of the tag, a line feed, the salt's bytes and the text's UTF-8 bytes", async (_name, vector) => {
    expect(await textDigest(vector.salt, vector.text)).toBe(vector.digest);
  });

  test("the longest vector is 5000 UTF-16 units, and the vectors hold a line feed, a character outside ASCII and one outside the basic plane", () => {
    expect(Math.max(...TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => vector.text.length))).toBe(5000);
    const all = TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => vector.text).join("");
    expect(all).toContain(LF);
    expect(all).toContain(E_ACUTE);
    expect(all).toContain(GRINNING);
  });

  test("another salt or another text gives another digest", async () => {
    const digests = await Promise.all([textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "one"), textDigest("a2".repeat(32), "one"), textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "one "), textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "One")]);
    expect(new Set(digests).size).toBe(4);
  });

  test("a salt that is not 32 bytes of lower-case hex is refused, never padded or folded", async () => {
    for (const salt of ["", "a1".repeat(31), "a1".repeat(33), "A1".repeat(32), "g1".repeat(32), ` ${"a1".repeat(32)}`]) {
      await expect(textDigest(salt, "text"), JSON.stringify(salt)).rejects.toThrow(TypeError);
    }
  });

  test("a text with a lone surrogate, which has no UTF-8 bytes, is refused rather than hashed as something else", async () => {
    const high = String.fromCharCode(0xd83d);
    const low = String.fromCharCode(0xde00);
    for (const text of [high, low, `a${high}b`, `${low}${high}`]) await expect(textDigest("a1".repeat(32), text)).rejects.toThrow(TypeError);
    // The pair itself is a character.
    await expect(textDigest("a1".repeat(32), `${high}${low}`)).resolves.toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  });
});

describe("snapshotText and snapshotDigest", () => {
  const post: SnapshotDigestInput = {
    salt: "ab".repeat(32),
    targetType: "post",
    targetId: "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a",
    takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.123Z",
    authorHandle: "ada",
    postState: "visible",
    postCreatedAt: "2026-10-01T08:30:00.000Z",
    replyToId: null,
    quoteOfId: "7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36",
    body: `Line one${LF}caf${E_ACUTE} ${GRINNING}`,
    media: [
      { id: "11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555", alt: "A cat", width: 1200, height: 800 },
      { id: "66666666-7777-4888-9999-aaaaaaaaaaaa", alt: null, width: 640, height: 480 },
    ],
    displayName: null,
    bio: null,
    handle: null,
  };
  const account: SnapshotDigestInput = {
    salt: "cd".repeat(32),
    targetType: "account",
    targetId: "8a3c7f0e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666",
    takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.000Z",
    authorHandle: "bob",
    postState: null,
    postCreatedAt: null,
    replyToId: null,
    quoteOfId: null,
    body: null,
    media: null,
    displayName: `Bob ${GRINNING}`,
    bio: "",
    handle: "bob",
  };
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  // The texts and the digests below were computed with Python's json and hashlib when they were written.
  const POST_TEXT =
    `{"authorHandle":"ada","bio":null,"body":"Line one${BS}ncaf${E_ACUTE} ${GRINNING}","displayName":null,"handle":null,` +
    `"media":[{"alt":"A cat","height":800,"id":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555","width":1200},{"alt":null,"height":480,"id":"66666666-7777-4888-9999-aaaaaaaaaaaa","width":640}],` +
    `"postCreatedAt":"2026-10-01T08:30:00.000Z","postState":"visible","quoteOfId":"7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36","replyToId":null,` +
    `"salt":"${"ab".repeat(32)}","takenAt":"2026-10-03T10:00:00.123Z","targetId":"3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a","targetType":"post","v":1}`;
  const POST_DIGEST = "cb995d11ed14e3c4e555c187d319a86506b263e98f924f59f2f7d5231a3bc6e6";
  const ACCOUNT_DIGEST = "41019b2a47d4ebad37cc8c5ad25f8d79a7232c4e3e705231f9e9ba1e02fb1f26";

  test("the tag names the version of the rule", () => {
    expect(SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_TAG).toBe("korbat.snapshot.v1");
  });

  test("the text is the sorted JSON of version 1 and the snapshot's fifteen members", () => {
    expect(snapshotText(post)).toBe(POST_TEXT);
    const parsed = JSON.parse(snapshotText(account)) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(Object.keys(parsed)).toEqual(["authorHandle", "bio", "body", "displayName", "handle", "media", "postCreatedAt", "postState", "quoteOfId", "replyToId", "salt", "takenAt", "targetId", "targetType", "v"]);
    expect(parsed).toEqual({ v: 1, ...account });
  });

  test("the digest is the sha256 of the tag, a line feed and that text", async () => {
    expect(await snapshotDigest(post)).toBe(POST_DIGEST);
    expect(await snapshotDigest(account)).toBe(ACCOUNT_DIGEST);
  });

  test("it round-trips the snapshot answer's JSON, whatever order and whatever else the answer carries", async () => {
    // As the console receives it: parsed from JSON, with members the digest does not cover, in another order.
    const sent = {
      id: "9d0f5e3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
      digest: POST_DIGEST,
      withheld: false,
      erasedAt: null,
      ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(post).reverse()),
      media: post.media!.map((image) => ({ height: image.height, width: image.width, note: "never part of a snapshot", alt: image.alt, id: image.id })),
    };
    const answer = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(sent)) as SnapshotDigestInput;
    expect(snapshotText(answer)).toBe(POST_TEXT);
    expect(await snapshotDigest(answer)).toBe(POST_DIGEST);
  });

  test("any member that changes gives another digest", async () => {
    const changed: SnapshotDigestInput[] = [
      { ...post, salt: "ac".repeat(32) },
      { ...post, takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.124Z" },
      { ...post, body: `${post.body} ` },
      { ...post, postState: "withheld" },
      { ...post, quoteOfId: null },
      { ...post, media: [post.media![1]!, post.media![0]!] },
      { ...post, media: [{ ...post.media![0]!, alt: "A dog" }, post.media![1]!] },
      { ...post, authorHandle: "adb" },
    ];
    const digests = await Promise.all([post, ...changed].map(snapshotDigest));
    expect(new Set(digests).size).toBe(changed.length + 1);
  });

  test("a time that is not the UTC string toISOString writes, to the millisecond, is refused", () => {
    for (const takenAt of ["2026-10-03T10:00:00Z", "2026-10-03T10:00:00.123456Z", "2026-10-03T12:00:00.123+02:00", "2026-10-03 10:00:00.123Z", ""]) {
      expect(() => snapshotText({ ...post, takenAt }), takenAt).toThrow(TypeError);
    }
    expect(() => snapshotText({ ...post, postCreatedAt: "2026-10-01T08:30:00Z" })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(snapshotText({ ...post, takenAt: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 3, 10, 0, 0, 123)).toISOString() })).toBe(POST_TEXT);
  });
});

describe("appealDeadline", () => {
  const at = (iso: string) => new Date(iso);
  const deadline = (iso: string) => appealDeadline(at(iso)).toISOString();

  test("six calendar months later, at the same UTC time", () => {
    expect(deadline("2026-10-03T10:15:30.250Z")).toBe("2027-04-03T10:15:30.250Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-07-15T00:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-07-01T23:59:59.999Z")).toBe("2027-01-01T23:59:59.999Z");
  });

  test("a day the sixth month lacks becomes that month's last day", () => {
    // 31 August plus six months is the end of February: the 28th, or the 29th in a leap year.
    expect(deadline("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-02-28T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-31T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-30T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-29T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-03-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-09-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-05-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-11-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-10-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-04-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-12-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-06-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    // A leap day itself moves to 29 August: August has the day.
    expect(deadline("2028-02-29T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-08-29T08:00:00.000Z");
  });

  test("it is computed in UTC: the last instants of a UTC month stay on that month's side", () => {
    expect(deadline("2026-08-31T23:59:59.999Z")).toBe("2027-02-28T23:59:59.999Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-03-01T00:00:00.000Z");
  });

  test("it leaves its argument as it was", () => {
    const informed = at("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z");
    appealDeadline(informed);
    expect(informed.toISOString()).toBe("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z");
  });
});

describe("ALERT_TEXTS (W.4): one text serves both legs, and it carries counts and times only (invariant 15)", () => {
  const now = new Date("2026-10-16T09:00:00.000Z");
  /** One set of facts for a kind: every count is `n`, every time the given instant. */
  const factsOf = (kind: AlertKind, n: number, time: string, over: Partial<Record<string, number | string | undefined>> = {}): AlertFacts => {
    const facts: Record<string, number | string> = {};
    for (const name of ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts) facts[name] = isTimeFact(name) ? time : n;
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(over)) {
      if (!ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts.includes(name)) continue;
      if (value === undefined) delete facts[name];
      else facts[name] = value;
    }
    return facts;
  };
  const DIGITS = /[0-9]/g;
  const all = (kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts) => {
    const r = renderAlert(kind, facts, now);
    return [r.title, r.sentence, r.todo ?? ""].join(" | ");
  };

  test("rendered with two sets of facts, every kind's title, sentence and line differ only in their digits", () => {
    for (const kind of ALERT_KIND_LIST) {
      // The flags of order_effected and order_opened chose a variant: both sets hold the same flags.
      const flags = { urgent: 0, unknown: 0 };
      // A day (3d's head alerts) prints as its date, so the two sets name two days: they differ in digits alone.
      const first = all(kind, factsOf(kind, 3, "2026-10-16T07:05:00.000Z", { ...flags, day: "2026-10-13T00:00:00.000Z" }));
      const second = all(kind, factsOf(kind, 1234, "2026-10-16T22:49:59.999Z", { ...flags, day: "2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z" }));
      expect(first.replace(DIGITS, ""), kind).toBe(second.replace(DIGITS, ""));
      expect(first, kind).not.toBe(second);
    }
  });

  test("no entry holds an @, a link or a placeholder that is neither a fact of its kind nor a number of ORDER_RULES, QUARANTINE_RULES, EDGE_WORDS or AUTOMATION_RULES", () => {
    for (const kind of ALERT_KIND_LIST) {
      const text = ALERT_TEXTS[kind];
      const words = [text.title, ...text.sentence.map((part) => part.text), text.todo ?? ""].join(" ");
      expect(words, kind).not.toContain("@");
      expect(words.toLowerCase(), kind).not.toContain("http");
      for (const name of alertPlaceholders(kind)) {
        expect([...ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts, ...Object.keys(ORDER_RULES), ...Object.keys(QUARANTINE_RULES), ...Object.keys(EDGE_WORDS), ...Object.keys(AUTOMATION_RULES)], `${kind}: {${name}}`).toContain(name);
      }
      // Every number a sentence of 3f prints comes from the facts or from ORDER_RULES: no digit is typed. 3c's burst
      // window is 3c's own number, which its push names as its mail does.
      if (ALERT_KINDS[kind].mail !== "own") expect(words.replace(/[{][a-zA-Z]+[}]/g, ""), kind).not.toMatch(DIGITS);
    }
  });

  test("a time prints as 14:05 UTC, with the day when it is not the day of the alert", () => {
    expect(alertTime("2026-10-16T14:05:59.000Z", now)).toBe("14:05 UTC");
    expect(alertTime("2026-10-15T23:59:00.000Z", now)).toBe("2026-10-15 23:59 UTC");
    expect(alertTime("2026-10-17T00:00:00.000Z", now)).toBe("2026-10-17 00:00 UTC");
  });

  test("the words of the kinds Task 1 sends, as W.4 has them", () => {
    const mail = renderAlert("contact_mail", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }, now);
    expect(mail).toEqual({
      title: "Mail at the contact point",
      sentence: "Mail at the authorities' contact point, received 08:05 UTC. If it is a removal order it is due 09:05 UTC.",
      todo: `Read it in the mail host's app, never in korbat, and with it every other new message there: further mail within ${ORDER_RULES.quietMinutes} minutes raises no alarm of its own. Then open Contact point in the staff console. What ends this message's alarms is handling it there: opening an order from it, or closing it.`,
    });
    // A restart of an order's clock has no time of receipt.
    expect(renderAlert("contact_mail", { dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }, now).sentence).toBe("A removal order's hour has started again: due 09:05 UTC.");
    expect(renderAlert("contact_mail_escalated", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "Nobody has answered: mail at the contact point",
      sentence: "Nobody has answered the mail that arrived at the authorities' contact point at 08:05 UTC. If it is a removal order it is due 09:05 UTC.",
      todo: "This went to every staff phone. Whoever reads it first acts, and tells the others.",
    });
    const due = renderAlert("order_due", { dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z", minutesLeft: 15 }, now);
    expect(due.title).toBe("15 minutes left");
    expect(due.sentence).toBe("A removal order, or mail that may be one, is due 09:05 UTC: 15 minutes are left and it is not carried out in full.");
    expect(due.todo).toBe(
      "Give effect now, to every post the order names. Only if the order has a manifest error, or lacks what you need to find the content, send Annex III and record it: that is no way to stop this alarm. If nobody can act in time: the README, When nobody can act within the hour.",
    );
    expect(renderAlert("mailbox_unreachable", { since: "2026-10-15T23:00:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "The contact point cannot be read",
      sentence: "korbat has not been able to read the contact-point mailbox since 2026-10-15 23:00 UTC.",
      todo: `Mail that arrives there raises no alert now. Check the mailbox in the mail host's app until this is repaired; an order you find there is opened in the console under Orders, with "The message is not listed". The operator checks the password and the mail host.`,
    });
    expect(renderAlert("alert_channel_down", { since: "2026-10-16T08:57:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "Phone alerts are down",

 * The words a report's sender reads for an outcome, and the console's fixed drafts for a seal (3c design, section 10).
 * Each table is the one place its words are written: the mails, the status page, the app's list and the console take
 * them from here, so this file pins every word once.
 */
const RULE = { id: "R1", title: "No sexual or pornographic content" };

/** One item's facts, plain unless a test says otherwise: a post that quotes nothing, answered by a decision that saw its images. */
const words = (outcome: ItemOutcome, facts: Partial<OutcomeWordsInput> = {}): string =>
  outcomeWords({ outcome, rule: outcome === "restricted_rule" ? RULE : null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null, ...facts });

describe("the outcome phrases", () => {

    expect(Object.keys(OUTCOME_PHRASES).sort()).toEqual([...ITEM_OUTCOMES].sort());
    expect(OUTCOME_PHRASES).toEqual({
      restricted_rule: "access restricted: it breaks korbat rule {rule} ({title})",
      restricted_legal: "access restricted: korbat found it illegal",
      no_violation: "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal",
      not_evident:
        "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules, and whether it is illegal cannot be seen without a detailed legal examination; a court or an authority can order its removal",
      not_available: "no action: the link names nothing korbat can show (checked automatically)",
      partly_reversed: "korbat reversed part of its decision to restrict it",
      reversed: "korbat reversed its decision to restrict it",
    });
  });

  test("the sentences that follow an outcome, and the phrases of the path for child sexual abuse material, word for word", () => {
    expect(ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN).toBe("It was already not shown on korbat, so nothing changed now; korbat's restriction stays in force should that change.");
    expect(ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE).toBe("This answer concerns the account's display name and bio. korbat decides about its posts and images in cases of their own and does not report those here.");
    expect(QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE).toBe(
      "This answer concerns this post's own text and images. korbat decides about the post it quotes, shown inside its card, in a case of its own and does not report that here.",
    );
    expect(ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE).toBe(
      "This answer concerns the account's display name and bio and, taken together, the images on its posts. korbat decides about single posts of the account, and about what its posts say, in cases of their own and does not report those here.",
    );
    expect(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES).toEqual({
      sealed: "access restricted: korbat sealed its images without opening them. They are shown to nobody, their author included, and are kept for the authorities.",
      no_action:

    });
    expect(SUSPECT_NO_SEAL).toBe("No image was sealed; korbat's staff do not open images reported this way.");
    expect(UNSEEN_NO_ACTION).toBe(
      "no action for now: when korbat decided, its staff could not open this post's images, because a report of another kind about them was waiting or they were sealed. If your report is about an image, ask for a re-examination.",
    );
  });
});

describe("outcomeWords: one item's outcome as its sender reads it", () => {
  test("an ordinary item reads its outcome's phrase, a rule's with its id and title, and ends in one full stop", () => {
    expect(words("restricted_rule")).toBe("access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content).");
    expect(words("restricted_legal")).toBe("access restricted: korbat found it illegal.");
    expect(words("no_violation")).toBe("no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal.");

    expect(words("reversed")).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.reversed}.`);
    // A phrase that fills nothing in never keeps a placeholder, and no outcome ends in two full stops.
    for (const outcome of ITEM_OUTCOMES) {

      }

  test("a restriction under a rule that is not named is refused: the phrase would keep its placeholder", () => {

      for (const scope of [null, "account", "account_suspect"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { scope }), `${outcome} ${String(scope)}`).not.toContain(QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE);

  });

  test("ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE follows the outcome of exactly the items about an account that are suspect or that a sealing decision answered, a rule report merged into a sealed account case among them", () => {
    for (const outcome of ITEM_OUTCOMES) {

      for (const scope of [null, "account", "quote"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { scope }), `${outcome} ${String(scope)}`).not.toContain(ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE);
    }
    // A rule report about an account that an answer with a seal answered: the sealed phrase, then the scope.
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { sealed: true, scope: "account_suspect" })).toBe(`${SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed} ${ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE}`);
  });

  test("a suspect item is worded from SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES, never from the four words for a finding alone", () => {
    expect(words("no_violation", { suspect: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_action);
    expect(words("not_evident", { suspect: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_action);
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { suspect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
    expect(words("restricted_legal", { suspect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
    // Answered by a measure on the post's text without a seal: the phrase of that finding, then that no image was sealed.
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { suspect: true })).toBe(`access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content). ${SUSPECT_NO_SEAL}`);
    expect(words("restricted_legal", { suspect: true })).toBe(`access restricted: korbat found it illegal. ${SUSPECT_NO_SEAL}`);

describe("the console's fixed drafts for a seal", () => {
  test("SEAL_DRAFTS holds its eight texts, word for word", () => {
    expect(SEAL_DRAFTS).toEqual({
      facts: {
        notice_post: "korbat received a notice that reports images of this post as child sexual abuse material.",
        notice_account: "korbat received a notice that reports this account for child sexual abuse material. It does not say which images, so korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
        notice_added: "korbat received a notice about content on korbat that shows this post's images and reports them as child sexual abuse material.",
        finding_post: "A moderator reported images of this post as possible child sexual abuse material.",
        finding_account: "A moderator reported images on this account's posts as possible child sexual abuse material. korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
        finding_added: "A moderator reported content on korbat that shows this post's images as possible child sexual abuse material.",
      },
      reason: {
        deciding: "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. It hides them from everyone, you included, until an admin has answered the report.",
        final:
          "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. An admin found the report credible enough to keep the images sealed and to report them to the police, who can assess them.",
      },
    });
    expect(Object.keys(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts).length + Object.keys(SEAL_DRAFTS.reason).length).toBe(8);
  });

  test("none says that korbat found the images to be such material, and each reason says that staff do not open them", () => {
    for (const text of [...Object.values(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts), ...Object.values(SEAL_DRAFTS.reason)]) {
      expect(text).not.toMatch(/korbat found|is child sexual abuse material|are child sexual abuse material/);
    }
    for (const text of Object.values(SEAL_DRAFTS.reason)) expect(text).toContain("korbat's staff do not open images reported this way");
    // The two drafts for an added item never say that this post was reported, and name no other post.
    for (const text of [SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_added, SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_added]) expect(text).not.toMatch(/of this post as|this post was|quot/);
  });

  test("the facts draft follows the suspect items the decision considers: a notice when any came from a user, the added form when every one was added by korbat, else by the case's target", () => {
    const item = (source: "user" | "finding", added = false) => ({ source, added });
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("user")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("account", [item("user")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_account);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("finding")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_post);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("account", [item("finding")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_account);
    // A notice among findings makes it a notice's draft.
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("finding"), item("user")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post);
    // Every item added for a quoted post (or a re-examination of one): the added form; one named item among them: the post's.
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("user", true), item("user", true)])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_added);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("finding", true)])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_added);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("user", true), item("finding")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post);
    expect(() => sealFactsDraft("post", [])).toThrow(/suspect item/);
  });
});

describe("FindingRequest", () => {
  const finding = { target: { kind: "post", id: POST }, ground: "rule", ruleId: "R1", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" };

  test("a moderator's finding cites a korbat rule, R2 among them, about a post, an account or a korbat link", () => {
    for (const ruleId of ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"]) expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId }).success, ruleId).toBe(true);
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "account", handle: "@Some_one" } }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(FindingRequest.parse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "account", handle: "@Some_one" } }).target).toEqual({ kind: "account", handle: "some_one" });
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "link", url: "https://korbat.example/post/" + POST } }).success).toBe(true);
  });

  test("it has no other ground than a rule: a finding never alleges illegality and never goes the path that records no sender", () => {
    for (const ground of ["illegal", "csam", "order", "law", ""]) expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ground }).success, ground).toBe(false);
    const { ground: _ground, ...withoutGround } = finding;
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse(withoutGround).success).toBe(false);
    // The members of the other grounds are refused, never ignored.
    for (const extra of [{ explanation: "words" }, { bonaFide: true }, { citedLaw: "a law" }, { keyword: "csam" }, { name: "A" }, { email: "a@b.example" }, { turnstileToken: "t" }]) {
      expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ...extra }).success, Object.keys(extra)[0]).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId: "R7" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId: null }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("its category is one of the Transparency Database's, but not the one that says a notifier was not sure", () => {

    expect(FINDING_CATEGORIES).toHaveLength(TDB_CATEGORIES.length - 1);

  });

});

describe("a saved text", () => {
  const save = { kind: "note", text: "Art. 18 check: no suspicion", salt: HEX, digest: HEX };

  test("is of one of the seven kinds, the recorded choice not to seal among them, with a 32-byte salt and a digest in lower-case hex", () => {
    expect(STAFF_TEXT_KINDS).toEqual(["facts", "reason", "legal_reference", "review_reason", "reveal_reason", "note", "seal_declined"]);
    for (const kind of STAFF_TEXT_KINDS) expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, kind }).success, kind).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, kind: "statement" }).success).toBe(false);
    for (const bad of [HEX.toUpperCase(), HEX.slice(2), `${HEX}00`, "", "g".repeat(64)]) {
      expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, salt: bad }).success, `salt ${bad}`).toBe(false);
      expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, digest: bad }).success, `digest ${bad}`).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, caseId: CASE }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the request's schema lets any text through: what a text must be is the route's to refuse, with a code of its own", () => {
    // A text that is too long or holds a control character is answered text_invalid, not invalid_request.
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: "x".repeat(STAFF_TEXT_MAX + 1) }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: `a${String.fromCharCode(7)}b` }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: 5 }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("staffTextProblem: a well-formed text of at most 5000 UTF-16 units, with no control character but the line feed and no invisible direction or zero-width character", () => {
    expect(STAFF_TEXT_MAX).toBe(5000);
    const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
    expect(staffTextProblem(`two${LF}lines`)).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("")).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("x".repeat(5000))).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("x".repeat(5001))).toBe("too_long");
    // An emoji is two units: 2500 of them fit, and one more unit does not.
    const emoji = String.fromCodePoint(0x1f600);
    expect(staffTextProblem(emoji.repeat(2500))).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem(`${emoji.repeat(2500)}x`)).toBe("too_long");
    // Half of a surrogate pair has no UTF-8 bytes.
    expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(0xd83d)}b`)).toBe("malformed");
    expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(0xde00)}`)).toBe("malformed");
    // NUL and every other C0 control but the line feed.
    for (let code = 0; code < 32; code++) {
      expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBe(code === 10 ? null : "control");
    }
    // The invisible direction and spacing characters the notice texts refuse too; the joiners scripts and emoji need stay.
    for (const code of [0x202a, 0x202e, 0x2066, 0x2069, 0x200b, 0x2060, 0xfeff]) expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBe("format");
    for (const code of [0x200c, 0x200d]) expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem(`r${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)}sum${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)}`)).toBeNull();
  });

  test("the answers: the stored text's id and digest, the person's own drafts with their salts, and a snapshot's id and digest, never content", () => {
    expect(StaffTextSaved.parse({ id: CASE, digest: HEX })).toEqual({ id: CASE, digest: HEX });
    const draft = { id: CASE, kind: "facts", text: "The post names a home address.", salt: HEX, digest: HEX, createdAt: TIME };
    expect(StaffTextsResponse.parse({ texts: [draft] }).texts).toEqual([draft]);
    expect(Object.keys(StaffSnapshotTaken.parse({ id: CASE, digest: HEX, body: "content", media: [] }))).toEqual(["id", "digest"]);
  });
});

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { actionKind } from "../src/schema/moderation";

/**
 * The rule for the new values of action_kind (3e design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1).
 * drizzle's migrator runs every pending migration in one transaction, and a value that ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE added
 * cannot be used as an enum literal before that transaction commits (SQLSTATE 55P04) in anything that is parsed when it
 * is created or run: a view, an SQL-language function, a check, a default, an index predicate, a plain statement. Only a
 * PL/pgSQL body is parsed when it is first called, which no migration statement does. So in 3e's migrations a new value
 * appears as a literal only inside a PL/pgSQL function's body, and everywhere else a kind is compared as text
 * (`kind::text = 'strike'`). This test reads 3e's migration files and refuses any other use.
 *
 * The SQL is read statement by statement, its comments dropped, and every run of white space made one space, so the
 * patterns below need no escapes.
 */

const MIGRATIONS = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../migrations");

/** 3c's twelve kinds come first in the enum; 3e's ten follow them, and 3f's two follow those (read below). */
const OLD_KINDS = 12;
const KINDS_3E = 10;
const NEW_KINDS: readonly string[] = actionKind.enumValues.slice(OLD_KINDS, OLD_KINDS + KINDS_3E);

/** 3e's first migration: 3c ended at 0019_redaction_scope, so 3e's migrations are 0020 and after. */
const FIRST_3E_MIGRATION = 20;

const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
const BREAKPOINT = "--> statement-breakpoint";

/** The journal's entries of 3e's migrations, oldest first. */
function migrationsOf3e(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {
  const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
  return journal.entries.filter((entry) => entry.idx >= FIRST_3E_MIGRATION);
}

/** A statement with its line comments dropped: a comment may name a kind in any words it likes. */
function withoutComments(statement: string): string {
  return statement
    .split(NEWLINE)
    .map((line) => {
      const at = line.indexOf("--");
      return at < 0 ? line : line.slice(0, at);
    })
    .join(NEWLINE);
}

/** Every run of white space (a code point up to the space) as one space, trimmed. */
function flat(text: string): string {
  return [...text]
    .map((char) => (char.charCodeAt(0) <= 32 ? " " : char))
    .join("")
    .split(" ")
    .filter((word) => word !== "")
    .join(" ");
}

/**
 * A statement with the body of a PL/pgSQL function blanked, so that only what is parsed at once is left: a statement that
 * creates a function in LANGUAGE plpgsql keeps its signature and loses what lies between its outer dollar quotes. A DO
 * block keeps its body: it runs inside the migration, and its literals are parsed then.
 */
function withoutPlpgsqlBody(statement: string): string {
  const upper = statement.toUpperCase();
  const creates = upper.startsWith("CREATE FUNCTION") || upper.startsWith("CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION");
  if (!creates || !upper.includes("LANGUAGE PLPGSQL")) return statement;
  const open = statement.indexOf("$$");
  const close = statement.lastIndexOf("$$");
  if (open < 0 || close <= open) return statement;
  return `${statement.slice(0, open + 2)} ${statement.slice(close)}`;
}

/**
 * The places where a literal is compared as text: `::text` followed by `=`, `<>`, `IN (` or `= ANY (ARRAY[` and then a
 * list of quoted words. A new kind's literal there is a text, and parses whatever the enum holds.
 */
const TEXT_COMPARISON = /::text ?(?:=|<>|!=|in ?[(]|= ?any ?[(] ?array ?[[]) ?'[a-z_]+'(?: ?, ?'[a-z_]+')*/gi;

/** The statement that adds a value names it, as a label and not as a literal of the enum. */
const ADDED_VALUE = /alter type [^ ]+ add value '[a-z_]+'/gi;

/** Every use of a new kind's literal in the SQL that is outside a PL/pgSQL body and not compared as text, each with its context. */
function enumLiteralViolations(sqlText: string, kinds: readonly string[] = NEW_KINDS): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  const literal = new RegExp(`'(${kinds.join("|")})'`, "g");
  for (const statement of sqlText.split(BREAKPOINT)) {
    const scanned = withoutPlpgsqlBody(flat(withoutComments(statement)));
    const allowed: [number, number][] = [];
    for (const pattern of [TEXT_COMPARISON, ADDED_VALUE]) {
      for (const match of scanned.matchAll(pattern)) allowed.push([match.index, match.index + match[0].length]);
    }
    for (const match of scanned.matchAll(literal)) {
      const at = match.index;
      const castToText = /^ ?::text(?![a-z_])/i.test(scanned.slice(at + match[0].length));
      if (castToText || allowed.some(([from, to]) => at >= from && at < to)) continue;
      violations.push(scanned.slice(Math.max(0, at - 60), at + match[0].length + 20));
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the enum-literal rule of 3e's migrations", () => {
  test("action_kind's new values are the ten of 3e, after 3c's twelve", () => {
    expect(NEW_KINDS).toEqual(["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting"]);
  });

  test("3e's migrations are there: the schema (0020) and standing_ledger (0021) at least", () => {
    const tags = migrationsOf3e().map((entry) => entry.tag);
    expect(tags.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(tags[1]).toBe("0021_standing_ledger");
  });

  test("no file of 3e names a new kind as a literal outside a PL/pgSQL body", () => {
    for (const entry of migrationsOf3e()) {
      const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
      expect(enumLiteralViolations(text), entry.tag).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  test("the files of 3e do name the new kinds, inside PL/pgSQL bodies, so the test reads what it should", () => {
    const ledger = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${migrationsOf3e()[1]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    // The same file read without blanking the bodies would hold many: the bodies are where the kinds are used.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(ledger.split("LANGUAGE plpgsql").join("LANGUAGE sql")).length).toBeGreaterThan(20);
  });

  test("a deliberate violation of each kind is caught, and the allowed forms are not", () => {
    // Caught: a view, an SQL function, a check and an index predicate that name a new kind as the enum, and a cast.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind IN ('suspend', 'terminate')) $$;`)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TABLE decision_actions ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (kind <> 'overrule');`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE INDEX i ON decision_actions (created_at) WHERE kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`SELECT 'lift_reporting'::public.action_kind;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // A DO block runs inside the migration: its body is no exemption.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Two statements: the second's violation is found although the first is a PL/pgSQL function.
    const two = `CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1; END $$;${BREAKPOINT}${NEWLINE}CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'suspend';`;
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(two)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Allowed: a comparison as text, a cast to text, any literal inside a PL/pgSQL body, an old kind, a comment, and the
    // statement that adds the value.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind::text = 'strike' AND a.kind::text IN ('suspend', 'terminate');`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 'strike'::text AS k;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'remove';`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`-- a.kind = 'strike' in a comment${NEWLINE}SELECT 1;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TYPE "public"."action_kind" ADD VALUE 'strike';`)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * 3f (design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1): the migration orders adds eight values to seven
 * enums: action_kind's disable_by_order and reinstate_by_order, `order` to decision_kind, decision_source and intake_kind,

const VALUES_3F: readonly string[] = ["disable_by_order", "reinstate_by_order", "order", "authority", "disabled"];

/** The journal's entries from the migration that adds 3f's values, oldest first. */
function migrationsFromOrders(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {

import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { is, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { PgDialect, PgTable, getTableConfig, pgTable } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";

import * as schema from "../src/schema/index";

const tables = Object.values(schema).filter((v) => is(v, PgTable)) as PgTable[];
const byName = new Map(tables.map((t) => [getTableConfig(t).name, getTableConfig(t)]));

describe("auth schema", () => {
  test("auth tables live in the auth schema", () => {
    for (const name of ["users", "devices", "sessions", "email_codes", "passkeys", "auth_events"]) {
      expect(byName.get(name)?.schema, name).toBe("auth");
    }
