```ts
};

/** The daily passkey bound as the API details it: 5 added in a day, and the seconds until the day has a slot again. */
function dailyPasskeyBound(details: unknown): number | null {
  const bound = details as { reason?: unknown; retryAfter?: unknown } | null;
  return bound && typeof bound === "object" && bound.reason === "daily" && typeof bound.retryAfter === "number" && bound.retryAfter > 0 ? bound.retryAfter : null;
}

/** The message for a code; `details` is what the server sent beside it, which turns the daily passkey bound into its wait in hours. */
export function messageFor(code: string, fallback?: string, details?: unknown): string {
  const wait = code === "passkey_limit" ? dailyPasskeyBound(details) : null;
  if (wait !== null) {
    const hours = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(wait / 3600));
    return `You added 5 passkeys today. You can add another in about ${hours === 1 ? "1 hour" : `${hours} hours`}.`;
  }
  return MESSAGES[code as keyof typeof MESSAGES] ?? fallback ?? "Something went wrong. Try again.";
}

/**
 * The codes worded here rather than by the server: validation and internal errors, whose server messages are technical;
 * the passkey bounds, whose daily wait is worded from the details; and (3e's review, people7) a report refused for the
 * restriction of reporting and a reply that is not open, whose screens print the app's own sentences of the design.
 */
function localWording(code: string): boolean {
  return code === "invalid_request" || code === "internal" || code === "passkey_limit" || code === "reporting_restricted" || code === "reply_not_open" || code === "objection_not_open";
}

/** The message to show for any thrown value. */
export function errorMessage(err: unknown): string {
  return err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : "Something went wrong. Try again.";
}

function readCookie(name: string): string | undefined {
  const cookies = web.document?.cookie;
  if (!cookies) return undefined;
  for (const part of cookies.split("; ")) {
    const separator = part.indexOf("=");
    if (part.slice(0, separator) === name) return decodeURIComponent(part.slice(separator + 1));
  }
  return undefined;
}

const BASE64URL = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_";

/** 32 random bytes as unpadded base64url (43 characters). */
function randomDeviceId(): string {
  const bytes = web.crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(33));
  let out = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 3) {
    const n = (bytes[i]! << 16) | (bytes[i + 1]! << 8) | bytes[i + 2]!;
    out += BASE64URL[(n >> 18) & 63]! + BASE64URL[(n >> 12) & 63]! + BASE64URL[(n >> 6) & 63]! + BASE64URL[n & 63]!;
  }
  return out.slice(0, 43);
}

/** A random id created once per browser. The server stores only a keyed hash of it. */
export function deviceId(): string {
  try {
    const existing = web.localStorage?.getItem(DEVICE_KEY);
    if (existing && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22,64}$/.test(existing)) return existing;
    const created = randomDeviceId();
    web.localStorage?.setItem(DEVICE_KEY, created);
    return created;
  } catch {
    return randomDeviceId();
  }
}

export const platform: "web" | "ios" | "android" = Platform.OS === "ios" || Platform.OS === "android" ? Platform.OS : "web";

interface RequestOptions<T> {
  method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  json?: unknown;
  /** A raw body sent as it is, with its declared type: how an image is uploaded. */
  raw?: { type: string; body: Blob };
  /** Schema for a JSON response body. Omit for 204 responses. */
  schema?: z.ZodType<T>;
}

/**
 * Calls the API with the session cookie and answers with the raw response, for a body that is not
 * JSON (the account export's ZIP). State-changing requests echo the CSRF cookie in X-CSRF-Token; the
 * session cookie itself is HttpOnly and never readable here. A failed call throws an ApiError.
 */
export async function apiResponse(path: string, options: Omit<RequestOptions<unknown>, "schema"> = {}): Promise<Response> {
  const method = options.method ?? (options.json === undefined && options.raw === undefined ? "GET" : "POST");
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {};
  if (options.json !== undefined) headers["content-type"] = "application/json";
  if (options.raw) headers["content-type"] = options.raw.type;
  if (method !== "GET") {
    const csrf = readCookie(CSRF_COOKIE);
    if (csrf) headers["x-csrf-token"] = csrf;
  }

  let res: Response;
  try {
    res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}${path}`, {
      method,
      headers,
      credentials: "include",
      body: options.raw ? options.raw.body : options.json === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(options.json),
    });
  } catch {
    throw new ApiError(0, "network", messageFor("network"));
  }

  if (!res.ok) {
    if (res.status === 401 && !path.startsWith("/api/auth/") && path !== "/api/me") onUnauthenticated?.();
    const parsed = ErrorEnvelope.safeParse(await res.json().catch(() => null));
    const code = parsed.success ? parsed.data.error.code : "internal";
    const details = parsed.success ? parsed.data.error.details : undefined;
    // 3e: a write refused for a running suspension: /me is read again, so the screens say until when.
    if (res.status === 403 && code === "account_suspended") onSuspended?.();
    // The server's message is written for people and can be more specific than the generic text for
    // its code ("Two-factor setup expired. Start again."). Only the codes localWording names use the
    // local wording.
    const local = localWording(code) || !parsed.success;
    // Retry-After is whole seconds: on a rate limit, and on the handle cooldown, where it says when the next change is allowed.
    const retryAfter = Number(res.headers.get("retry-after"));
    throw new ApiError(res.status, code, local ? messageFor(code, undefined, details) : parsed.data.error.message, Number.isFinite(retryAfter) && retryAfter > 0 ? retryAfter : undefined, details);
  }
  return res;
}

/** Calls the API as `apiResponse` does and parses the JSON answer with `schema`; omit it for a 204 response. */
export async function api<T = void>(path: string, options: RequestOptions<T> = {}): Promise<T> {
  const res = await apiResponse(path, options);
  if (!options.schema) return undefined as T;
  return options.schema.parse(await res.json());
}

export async function fetchHealth(): Promise<HealthResponse> {
  return api("/api/health", { schema: HealthResponse });
}
```

```ts
import { ORDER_TEXTS } from "./orders";

/**
 * Reports, notices and moderation cases in the app (3c design, section 9): the calls, and the rules the screens share.
 * Everything that decides is a plain function here, so a test can call it: what a report's address carries, what the
 * form sends, which sentence a failure gets, and what stands beside an item's outcome.

 * The users' contact address, which Expo inlines into the web bundle at export time (WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env; the
 * web image refuses to build without one). The report form names it when the form itself cannot be used, and the terms
 * page shows it.
 */
export const CONTACT_EMAIL = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL ?? "";

/**
 * What an appeal or a request for a re-examination carries of what its person typed: the statement, trimmed, when
 * something was written, and nothing otherwise. It is optional and free of form.
 */
export function statementOf(written: string): { statement?: string } {
  const statement = written.trim();
  return statement.length > 0 ? { statement } : {};
}

/** The moderation endpoints the app calls, typed by the shared contracts. Cookies and CSRF are handled by `api`. */
export const moderation = {

  send: (request: NoticeRequest) => api("/api/notices", { json: request, schema: NoticeResponse }),
  /** Where a notice stands. The token travels in the body of a POST, never in an address. */
  status: (ref: string, token: string) => api("/api/notices/status", { json: { ref, token }, schema: NoticeStatus }),
  /** The status page's buttons, for which only the token of a mail's link works. */
  contact: (ref: string, token: string, choice: "confirm" | "stop") => api("/api/notices/contact", { json: { ref, token, choice } }),
  cases: (cursor?: string) => api(`/api/moderation/cases${query(cursor)}`, { schema: AuthorCasesPage }),
  decision: (id: string) => api(`/api/moderation/decisions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, { schema: DecisionView }),
  reports: (cursor?: string) => api(`/api/moderation/reports${query(cursor)}`, { schema: ReportsPage }),
  /** 3d Task 2: the notices about the account's posts that are not decisions, newest first: the releases of its sealed images. */
  notices: (cursor?: string) => api(`/api/moderation/notices${query(cursor)}`, { schema: AuthorNoticesPage }),
  /** 3d Task 2: one release's notice, for its author alone; not_found for anyone else, and while it may not be told yet. */
  release: (id: string) => api(`/api/moderation/releases/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, { schema: ReleaseNoticeView }),
  resumeReportMail: () => api("/api/moderation/report-mail/resume", { method: "POST" }),
  /** The author's appeal of a decision about them. The answer is the decision as it now reads, with the appeal waiting. */
  appeal: (id: string, statement: string) => api(`/api/moderation/decisions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/appeal`, { json: statementOf(statement), schema: DecisionView }),
  /**
   * 3e Task 4: the person's reply to a decision that holds a suspension or a termination, with what they wrote, if
   * anything. The answer says when korbat received it and whether that was before the start.
   */
  reply: (id: string, statement: string) => api(`/api/moderation/decisions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/reply`, { json: statementOf(statement), schema: ReplyResponse }),
  /**
   * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 7.10 and 9.4): "Ask for a person" about a program's decision, with the one message its
   * subject writes. The answer is the decision as it now reads, with the request sent.
   */
  objection: (id: string, text: string) => api(`/api/moderation/decisions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/objection`, { json: { text }, schema: DecisionView }),
  /** A re-examination of an item of a notice, asked with the status page's token, which travels in the body of a POST. */
  reexamineNotice: (ref: string, token: string, position: number, statement: string) => api("/api/notices/reexamine", { json: { ref, token, position, ...statementOf(statement) }, schema: ReexamineResponse }),
  /** A re-examination of an item of a report the signed-in account sent, named by the id its list carries. */
  reexamineOwn: (itemId: string, statement: string) => api(`/api/moderation/items/${encodeURIComponent(itemId)}/reexamine`, { json: statementOf(statement), schema: ReexamineResponse }),
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what a report is opened on

/** A post, optionally with the one of its images that is meant, or a profile: what "Report" was pressed on. */
export type GivenTarget = Extract<NoticeTarget, { kind: "post" | "account" }>;

/** The report form's address: on its own, or opened on a post, on one image of a post, or on a profile. */
export function reportHref(on?: { post: string; media?: string } | { account: string }): string {
  if (!on) return "/report";
  if ("account" in on) return `/report?account=${encodeURIComponent(on.account)}`;
  return `/report?post=${encodeURIComponent(on.post)}${on.media ? `&media=${encodeURIComponent(on.media)}` : ""}`;
}

const one = (value: unknown): string | undefined => (typeof value === "string" && value.length > 0 ? value : undefined);

/** What the form's address names, or null when it names nothing the API would take: the form then asks for a link. */
export function givenTarget(params: { post?: unknown; media?: unknown; account?: unknown }): GivenTarget | null {
  const [post, media, account] = [one(params.post), one(params.media), one(params.account)];
  const parsed = post !== undefined ? NoticeTarget.safeParse({ kind: "post", id: post, ...(media !== undefined ? { mediaId: media } : {}) }) : account !== undefined ? NoticeTarget.safeParse({ kind: "account", handle: account }) : null;
  return parsed?.success && parsed.data.kind !== "link" ? parsed.data : null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the form

export type Ground = "rule" | "illegal" | "csam";

/** The category of an illegal-ground notice: one of the 14 the form shows, or "not specified" for someone who is not sure. */
export type NoticeCategoryChoice = TdbFormCategory | "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE";

/** What the person has filled in so far. */
export interface ReportDraft {
  ground: Ground | null;
  /** The rule of the rule ground; on the illegal ground, a rule it also breaks. */
  ruleId: ReportRuleId | null;
  explanation: string;
  category: NoticeCategoryChoice;
  citedLaw: string;
  bonaFide: boolean;
  keyword: CsamKeywordChoice | null;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  /** The item's link, when the form was opened without an item. */
  link: string;
  /** Up to nine more korbat links. */
  others: string[];
}

export const EMPTY_DRAFT: ReportDraft = {
  ground: null,
  ruleId: null,
  explanation: "",
  category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  citedLaw: "",
  bonaFide: false,
  keyword: null,
  name: "",
  email: "",
  link: "",
  others: [],
};

/** How many more links "Other items" takes. */
export const OTHER_LINKS_MAX = NOTICE_LIMITS.maxTargets - 1;

/** What the draft names, in order: the item the form was opened on or its link, then the other links that hold something. */
export function draftTargets(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null): NoticeTarget[] {
  const links = [...(given ? [] : [draft.link]), ...draft.others].map((url) => url.trim()).filter((url) => url.length > 0);
  return [...(given ? [given] : []), ...links.map((url) => ({ kind: "link" as const, url }))];
}

/** The handle a target names when it is a profile: an account, or a link to /u/<handle>. Null for anything else. */
function profileOf(target: NoticeTarget): string | null {
  if (target.kind === "account") return target.handle.toLowerCase();
  if (target.kind !== "link") return null;
  try {
    const match = /^[/]u[/]@?([A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20})[/]?$/.exec(new URL(target.url).pathname);
    return match ? match[1]!.toLowerCase() : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/** How many different profiles the targets name. */
export function profilesNamed(targets: readonly NoticeTarget[]): number {
  return new Set(targets.map(profileOf).filter((handle) => handle !== null)).size;
}

/**
 * Whether the form asks for the post or the image itself: on the anonymous path, for images, when the only item is a
 * profile. From a profile alone korbat cannot tell which image is meant. The form says so and never refuses the profile.
 */
export function profileOnly(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null): boolean {
  const targets = draftTargets(draft, given);
  return draft.ground === "csam" && (draft.keyword === "csam" || draft.keyword === "deepfake") && targets.length === 1 && profileOf(targets[0]!) !== null;
}

/** Whether the anonymous path's report names more profiles than one report may: the form says so before anything is sent. */
export function tooManyProfiles(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null): boolean {
  return draft.ground === "csam" && profilesNamed(draftTargets(draft, given)) > CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS;
}

const text = (value: string): string | undefined => (value.trim().length > 0 ? value.trim() : undefined);

/**
 * The request the draft makes, or the sentence that says what is still missing. A signed-out sender needs the human
 * check's token on every ground; a name and an address are sent only signed out and only on the illegal ground, since a
 * signed-in sender's contact is their account and the anonymous path asks for neither.
 */
export function noticeFrom(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null, sender: { signedIn: boolean; turnstileToken: string | null }): { request: NoticeRequest } | { problem: string } {
  const missing = REPORT_WORDS.missing;
  if (draft.ground === null) return { problem: missing.ground };
  const targets = draftTargets(draft, given);
  if (targets.length === 0) return { problem: missing.link };
  if (targets.some((target) => target.kind === "link" && !/^https?:[/][/]/i.test(target.url))) return { problem: missing.linkInvalid };
  const human = sender.signedIn ? {} : { turnstileToken: sender.turnstileToken ?? undefined };
  const explanation = text(draft.explanation);
  let request: unknown;
  if (draft.ground === "rule") {
    if (draft.ruleId === null) return { problem: missing.rule };
    request = { ground: "rule", ruleId: draft.ruleId, targets, ...(explanation ? { explanation } : {}), ...human };
  } else if (draft.ground === "illegal") {
    if (!explanation) return { problem: missing.whyIllegal };
    if (!draft.bonaFide) return { problem: missing.bonaFide };
    const [citedLaw, name, email] = [text(draft.citedLaw), text(draft.name), text(draft.email)];
    request = {
      ground: "illegal",
      targets,
      category: draft.category,
      ...(citedLaw ? { citedLaw } : {}),
      explanation,
      bonaFide: true,
      ...(draft.ruleId ? { ruleId: draft.ruleId } : {}),
      ...(!sender.signedIn && name ? { name } : {}),
      ...(!sender.signedIn && email ? { email } : {}),
      ...human,
    };
  } else {
    if (draft.keyword === null) return { problem: missing.keyword };
    if (tooManyProfiles(draft, given)) return { problem: REPORT_WORDS.oneProfile };
    request = { ground: "csam", targets, keyword: draft.keyword, ...(explanation ? { explanation } : {}), ...(draft.bonaFide ? { bonaFide: true } : {}), ...human };
  }
  if (!sender.signedIn && !sender.turnstileToken) return { problem: missing.human };
  const parsed = NoticeRequest.safeParse(request);
  return parsed.success ? { request: parsed.data } : { problem: missing.details };
}

/** The first sentence of a rule's text: the one line the form shows under its title. */
export function ruleLine(rule: Pick<Rule, "text">): string {
  const end = rule.text.indexOf(". ");
  return end === -1 ? rule.text : rule.text.slice(0, end + 1);
}

/** A wait as the form words it, from the answer's Retry-After: in minutes under an hour, in hours otherwise. */
export function waitWords(seconds: number | undefined): string {
  if (seconds === undefined || seconds >= 3600) {
    const hours = seconds === undefined ? 1 : Math.ceil(seconds / 3600);
    return hours === 1 ? "1 hour" : `${hours} hours`;
  }
  const minutes = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(seconds / 60));
  return minutes === 1 ? "1 minute" : `${minutes} minutes`;
}

/**
 * What the form shows for a failed send. Three failures get the form's own words, which name the users' contact address,
 * since for each the form itself is what does not work: the human check, the limits and an API that cannot take reports.
 * On the anonymous path each is followed by what a mail gives away. Anything else is the server's message, as elsewhere.
 */
export function reportFailure(err: unknown, anonymous: boolean, contact: string = CONTACT_EMAIL): string {
  if (!(err instanceof ApiError)) return errorMessage(err);
  let words: string | null = null;
  if (err.code === "human_check_failed") words = REPORT_WORDS.humanCheckFailed(contact);
  if (err.code === "rate_limited") words = REPORT_WORDS.rateLimited(waitWords(err.retryAfter), contact);
  if (err.code === "service_unavailable") words = REPORT_WORDS.unavailable(contact);
  if (words === null) return errorMessage(err);
  return anonymous ? `${words} ${REPORT_WORDS.mailShowsAddress}` : words;
}

/** What the appeal form and the re-examination control show for a failed request: the day's limit in words of its own, with the wait; anything else as elsewhere. */
export function dailyLimitFailure(err: unknown, limit: keyof typeof DAILY_LIMIT_WORDS): string {
  if (err instanceof ApiError && err.code === "rate_limited") return DAILY_LIMIT_WORDS[limit](waitWords(err.retryAfter));
  return errorMessage(err);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the status page

/** The status page's address for a notice, its token in the fragment, which no server is sent. */
export function statusLink(origin: string, ref: string, token: string): string {
  return `${origin}/notice/${ref}#t=${token}`;
}

/** The token a status page's address carries in its fragment, or null when the fragment holds none. */
export function fragmentToken(hash: string): string | null {
  return /^#t=([A-Za-z0-9_-]{43})$/.exec(hash)?.[1] ?? null;
}

/**
 * What stands beside one item on the status page and in Your reports (3c design, section 9, and the rule of 7.8 step 4):
 *   - `waiting`: nothing is released yet;
 *   - `final`: the outcome was changed on review or by a correction, or answers a re-examination: it is final within
 *     korbat. An answer given while nobody could open the post's images is never final: it leaves the re-examination
 *     unspent;
 *   - `reexamination`: the answer can still be examined again, until the item's date;
 *   - `courts`: any other decided outcome, which cannot be examined again.
 */
export function itemRedress(item: NoticeItemStatus): "waiting" | "final" | "reexamination" | "courts" {
  if (item.outcome === null) return "waiting";
  const unseenAnswer = item.unseen && (item.outcome === "no_violation" || item.outcome === "not_evident");
  if (item.changed || (item.reexamines && !unseenAnswer)) return "final";
  if (item.reexamination?.open) return "reexamination";
  return "courts";
}

/**
 * Whether asking for a re-examination of the item at `index` examines another item too (3c design, section 7.2): the
 * item is a report of child sexual abuse material that the sender named, and the item korbat added for the post it
 * quotes can be examined again as well. korbat then examines both, and the page says so beside the control.
 */
export function quotedExaminedToo(items: readonly NoticeItemStatus[], index: number): boolean {
  const item = items[index];
  if (!item || !item.suspect || item.quotedBy !== null || !item.reexamination?.open) return false;
  return items.some((other) => other.quotedBy === item.position && !other.reexamines && other.reexamination?.open === true);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the appeal's state

/**
 * What a pending appeal's line says on the decision's screen (3c design, section 7.7), from the decision's own data and
 * the API's two answers about its review, which name nobody:
 *   - an appeal of a decision that sealed images waits for the authorities' assessment, whoever could review it;
 *   - otherwise, while someone at korbat may review it, it waits for a reviewer;
 *   - when nobody may: for a review that is an admin's, that it waits for an admin, and that korbat has one while it
 *     has one; else that korbat has one moderator, or that none who took no part in the case is available now. The last
 *     gives no reason: a moderator may be unable to review through a relation to someone in the case.
 */
export function appealWaitWords(view: Pick<DecisionView, "measures" | "appeal">): string | null {
  const appeal = view.appeal;
  if (appeal === null || appeal.state !== "pending") return null;
  const waits = DECISION_WORDS.appealWaits;
  if (view.measures.some((measure) => measure.kind === "seal_media")) return waits.sealed;
  if (appeal.reviewer === "available") return DECISION_WORDS.appealWaiting;
  if (appeal.needsAdmin) return appeal.reviewer === "none_single_staff" ? `${waits.admin} ${waits.oneAdmin}` : waits.admin;
  return waits[appeal.reviewer];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- chips and times

/** The chip of the author's own withheld or removed post: "Under review: R4", "Removed: illegal content". */
export function chipText(decision: PostModeration): string {
  // 3f (design, section 9.1): [chip.order], a post a DSA order removed without withholding it from its author.
  if (decision.order === true) return ORDER_TEXTS.chip.order;
  const state = decision.interim ? CHIP_WORDS.underReview : CHIP_WORDS.removed;
  const ground = decision.legal ? CHIP_WORDS.illegal : decision.ruleId;
  const chip = ground ? `${state}: ${ground}` : state;
  // 3e (design, section 9.4): a removed post's chip names its strike while the strike stands and counts.
  return decision.strikeUntil ? STANDING_TEXTS.chip(chip, decision.strikeUntil) : chip;
}

/** A time as korbat's statements print it: the date and the minute in UTC. */
export function utcMinute(at: string): string {
  const iso = new Date(at).toISOString();
  return `${iso.slice(0, 10)} ${iso.slice(11, 16)} UTC`;
}
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { parseFormats, type MediaFormat } from "@korbat/media-protocol";

/** A blank value, as Compose passes an unset variable, counts as unset. */
const blankAsUnset = z.preprocess((value) => (value === "" ? undefined : value), z.string().optional());

const schema = z.object({
  NODE_ENV: z.enum(["development", "test", "production"]).default("development"),
  LOG_LEVEL: z.enum(["fatal", "error", "warn", "info", "debug", "trace", "silent"]).default("info"),
  /** The uploads volume, which this process may only read. */
  MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: z.string().min(1),
  /** The store volume, the only place this process writes. */
  MEDIA_STORE_DIR: z.string().min(1),
  MEDIA_FORMATS: z.string().optional(),
  VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED: z.string().optional(),
  /**
   * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 5 "The adapters" and 10.8): the R1 scorer. `off` (the default) scores nothing; `test`
   * answers 1 for the fixtures' marker and 0 otherwise; `onnx` is the real classifier, which this build does not carry.
   */
  R1_CLASSIFIER: blankAsUnset.pipe(z.enum(["off", "test", "onnx"]).default("off")),
  /** Caddy's switch of the app's site (3f), handed to the worker only so that a test adapter never runs on an open site. */
  APP_SITE: blankAsUnset.pipe(z.enum(["open", "closed"]).default("open")),
});

/** The refusal of a configuration: "Invalid environment:" and what is wrong, on a line of its own. */
const invalid = (message: string) => new Error(["Invalid environment:", message].join(String.fromCharCode(10)));

export interface Config {
  production: boolean;
  logLevel: z.infer<typeof schema>["LOG_LEVEL"];
  uploadsDir: string;
  storeDir: string;
  formats: MediaFormat[];
  /** 3d Task 6: the scorer this process runs; never a test scorer on an open site, and never one this build lacks. */
  r1Classifier: "off" | "test";
}

/**
 * The worker's whole configuration: two directories, the enabled formats, a log level and (3d) the scorer's setting with
 * the site's switch. It has no database URL, no Redis URL and no keys, by design. libvips reads VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED when
 * it loads, so it has to be in the environment before the process starts; production refuses to run without it.
 *
 * 3d (design, section 5, review ruling 11): in every environment, a test adapter is refused while APP_SITE is open, so
 * a stand-in never answers for a real classifier on a site people can reach; and `onnx` stops the process, since no
 * classifier is built in.
 */
export function loadConfig(env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env): Config {
  const result = schema.safeParse(env);
  if (!result.success) throw invalid(z.prettifyError(result.error));
  const production = result.data.NODE_ENV === "production";
  if (production && result.data.VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED === undefined) {
    throw invalid("VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED must be set before the worker starts");
  }
  const classifier = result.data.R1_CLASSIFIER;
  if (classifier === "onnx") throw invalid("R1_CLASSIFIER=onnx: no such adapter in this build; set R1_CLASSIFIER=off");
  if (classifier === "test" && result.data.APP_SITE === "open") {
    throw invalid("R1_CLASSIFIER=test is refused while APP_SITE is open: a test adapter answers only on a site that is closed");
  }
  return {
    production,
    logLevel: result.data.LOG_LEVEL,
    uploadsDir: result.data.MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR,
    storeDir: result.data.MEDIA_STORE_DIR,
    formats: parseFormats(result.data.MEDIA_FORMATS),
    r1Classifier: classifier,
  };
}
```

### Replace `apps/worker/src/index.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";
import pino from "pino";
import { HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS, storeLayout, uploadsLayout } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { loadConfig } from "./config";
import { WATCHDOG_MS, prepareStore, tick, writeHeartbeat, type LoopDeps } from "./loop";
import { configureDecoder, processImage } from "./pipeline";
import { scorerFrom } from "./score";

/**
 * The image worker. It reads uploads from one volume and writes WebP files, results and a
 * heartbeat to another, one image at a time. It has no network, no database and no queue: the two
 * volumes are everything it can reach. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-images-2b-design.md.
 */
const config = loadConfig();
const log = pino({ level: config.logLevel, base: undefined });
configureDecoder(config.formats);

// 3d Task 6: the R1 scorer of R1_CLASSIFIER, none while it is off; the configuration refused a test scorer on an open site.
const scorer = scorerFrom(config.r1Classifier);

const deps: LoopDeps = {
  uploads: uploadsLayout(config.uploadsDir),
  store: storeLayout(config.storeDir),
  formats: config.formats,
  log,
  now: Date.now,
  process: (path, formats) => processImage(path, formats, scorer),
  abort: (reason) => {
    log.fatal({ reason }, "watchdog: exiting so the container restarts");
    process.exit(1);
  },
  watchdogMs: WATCHDOG_MS,
};

await prepareStore(deps.store);
await writeHeartbeat(deps);
// The heartbeat has its own timer: decoding runs off the main thread, so it keeps beating during a long image.
const heartbeat = setInterval(() => void writeHeartbeat(deps).catch((err: unknown) => log.error({ err }, "heartbeat failed")), HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS);

let running = true;
const stop = (signal: string) => {
  log.info({ signal }, "stopping after the current image");
  running = false;
};
process.on("SIGTERM", () => stop("SIGTERM"));
process.on("SIGINT", () => stop("SIGINT"));

log.info({ formats: config.formats, r1Classifier: config.r1Classifier }, "worker started");
while (running) {
  const worked = await tick(deps).catch((err: unknown) => {
    log.error({ err }, "tick failed");
    return false;
  });
  if (!worked) await sleep(500);
}
clearInterval(heartbeat);
```

### Replace `apps/worker/src/loop.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { lstat, mkdir, open, readFile, readdir, rename, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { MAX_ATTEMPTS, RESULT_VERSION, isMediaId, resultFileId, type Heartbeat, type MediaFormat, type ResultFile, type StoreLayout, type UploadsLayout } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import type { Processed } from "./pipeline";

export interface LoopDeps {
  uploads: UploadsLayout;
  store: StoreLayout;
  formats: readonly MediaFormat[];
  log: Logger;
  now: () => number;
  /** The image pipeline. Tests pass a stand-in; the process passes processImage. */
  process: (path: string, formats: readonly MediaFormat[]) => Promise<Processed>;
  /** Ends the process when one upload takes too long. Docker restarts the container, and the attempt counter does the rest. */
  abort: (reason: string) => void;
  watchdogMs: number;
}

export const WATCHDOG_MS = 120_000;

/** Creates the store's directories and forgets files a crash left half written. */
export async function prepareStore(store: StoreLayout): Promise<void> {
  await rm(store.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
  for (const dir of [store.files, store.results, store.attempts, store.tmp]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
}

/** Write under tmp/, flush, rename: the API never sees half a file, and a finished file survives a power cut. */
async function writeAtomic(store: StoreLayout, target: string, data: string | Buffer): Promise<void> {
  const temp = path.join(store.tmp, randomUUID());
  const handle = await open(temp, "w");
  try {
    await handle.writeFile(data);
    await handle.sync();
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
  await rename(temp, target);
}

export async function writeHeartbeat(deps: Pick<LoopDeps, "store" | "now">): Promise<void> {
  const beat: Heartbeat = { v: 1, at: deps.now() };
  await writeAtomic(deps.store, deps.store.heartbeat, JSON.stringify(beat));
}

/** Names in a directory that are media ids and regular files. Anything else, a symlink included, is ignored. */
async function mediaFiles(dir: string): Promise<{ id: string; mtimeMs: number }[]> {
  const names = await readdir(dir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
  const found: { id: string; mtimeMs: number }[] = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    if (!isMediaId(name)) continue;
    const stats = await lstat(path.join(dir, name)).catch(() => null);
    if (stats?.isFile()) found.push({ id: name, mtimeMs: stats.mtimeMs });
  }
  return found.sort((a, b) => a.mtimeMs - b.mtimeMs || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
}

async function readAttempts(store: StoreLayout, id: string): Promise<number> {
  const text = await readFile(store.attempt(id), "utf8").catch(() => "0");
  const count = Number.parseInt(text, 10);
  return Number.isInteger(count) && count >= 0 ? count : MAX_ATTEMPTS;
}

const writeResult = (store: StoreLayout, result: ResultFile) => writeAtomic(store, store.result(result.id), JSON.stringify(result));

/**
 * A deletion request stays until the API sees the image gone and removes it, so this runs for the
 * same id on several ticks. It only acts while something is left, which makes repeats free, and it
 * also catches files that were written after the request arrived.
 */
async function handleDeletions(deps: LoopDeps): Promise<boolean> {
  let worked = false;
  for (const { id } of await mediaFiles(deps.uploads.deletions)) {
    const leftovers = [deps.store.imageDir(id), deps.store.result(id), deps.store.attempt(id)].filter((target) => existsSync(target));
    if (leftovers.length === 0) continue;
    for (const target of leftovers) await rm(target, { recursive: true, force: true });
    deps.log.info({ id }, "image deleted");
    worked = true;
  }
  return worked;
}

/** One upload, start to finish. The attempt is counted before any decoding, so a file that kills the process cannot loop. */
async function processOne(deps: LoopDeps, id: string): Promise<void> {
  const { store, uploads, log } = deps;
  const attempts = await readAttempts(store, id);
  if (attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
    await writeResult(store, { v: RESULT_VERSION, id, status: "failed", reason: "processing_failed" });
    log.warn({ id, attempts }, "upload failed: too many attempts");
    return;
  }
  await writeAtomic(store, store.attempt(id), String(attempts + 1));

  const started = deps.now();
  const watchdog = setTimeout(() => deps.abort(`upload ${id} took longer than ${deps.watchdogMs} ms`), deps.watchdogMs);
  let processed: Processed;
  try {
    processed = await deps.process(uploads.upload(id), deps.formats);
  } catch (err) {
    if (!existsSync(uploads.upload(id))) return; // The API withdrew the upload while it was being read.
    log.error({ id, err }, "processing threw; the upload will be tried again");
    return;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(watchdog);
  }

  if (!processed.ok) {
    await writeResult(store, { v: RESULT_VERSION, id, status: "failed", reason: processed.reason });
    log.info({ id, reason: processed.reason, ms: deps.now() - started }, "upload refused");
    return;
  }
  await mkdir(store.imageDir(id), { recursive: true });
  await writeAtomic(store, store.image(id, "large"), processed.large);
  await writeAtomic(store, store.image(id, "small"), processed.small);
  // The result is the commit point: it is written last, when both files are in place. 3d Task 6: version 2, with the
  // scorer's model and score while one runs. The score is not logged: it is a fact about an image the API alone keeps.
  await writeResult(store, {
    v: RESULT_VERSION,
    id,
    status: "ready",
    width: processed.width,
    height: processed.height,
    blurhash: processed.blurhash,
    ...(processed.r1 !== undefined ? { r1: processed.r1 } : {}),
  });
  log.info({ id, width: processed.width, height: processed.height, ms: deps.now() - started }, "upload processed");
}

/** A result or an attempt counter whose upload is gone has been consumed by the API, or belongs to an upload it withdrew. */
async function cleanResults(deps: LoopDeps): Promise<void> {
  for (const name of await readdir(deps.store.results).catch(() => [] as string[])) {
    const id = resultFileId(name);
    if (id && !existsSync(deps.uploads.upload(id))) await rm(deps.store.result(id), { force: true });
  }
  for (const id of await readdir(deps.store.attempts).catch(() => [] as string[])) {
    if (isMediaId(id) && !existsSync(deps.uploads.upload(id))) await rm(deps.store.attempt(id), { force: true });
  }
}

/**
 * One pass: deletions, then at most one upload, then result cleanup. Returns whether it did any
 * work, so the caller only sleeps when there was none.
 */
export async function tick(deps: LoopDeps): Promise<boolean> {
  let worked = await handleDeletions(deps);
  // An upload that already has a result is waiting for the API; one with a deletion request is not wanted any more.
  const pending = (await mediaFiles(deps.uploads.incoming)).filter(({ id }) => !existsSync(deps.store.result(id)) && !existsSync(deps.uploads.deletion(id)));
  const next = pending[0];
  if (next) {
    await processOne(deps, next.id);
    worked = true;
  }
  await cleanResults(deps);
  return worked;
}
```

### Replace `apps/worker/src/pipeline.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { closeSync, openSync, readSync } from "node:fs";
import { encode } from "blurhash";
import sharp from "sharp";
import type { MediaFailure } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { MAX_SIDE, PIXEL_CAP, SNIFF_BYTES, VARIANTS, isAnimatedPng, sniffImage, type ByteReader, type MediaFormat } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import type { Scorer } from "./score";

/**
 * Everything that touches the image decoder lives in this file. The decoder is the most
 * exploitable code korbat runs, so it only ever sees formats on an allowlist, only after the
 * file's first bytes said it is one of them, and only with a pixel cap it enforces from the header.
 */

/** libvips loader classes. Unblocking a parent class unblocks its file, buffer and source loaders. */
const LOADER: Record<MediaFormat, string> = {
  jpeg: "VipsForeignLoadJpeg",
  png: "VipsForeignLoadPng",
  webp: "VipsForeignLoadWebp",
  gif: "VipsForeignLoadNsgif",
  avif: "VipsForeignLoadHeif",
};

/** What sharp's metadata calls each format. AVIF arrives as "heif" with AV1 compression. */
const METADATA_FORMAT: Record<MediaFormat, string> = { jpeg: "jpeg", png: "png", webp: "webp", gif: "gif", avif: "heif" };

/**
 * Blocks every loader libvips has (the prebuilt binary also carries SVG and TIFF), then unblocks the
 * enabled formats. libvips ignores a class name it does not know, so a typo here would not raise an
 * error; the tests prove that every enabled format decodes and that SVG and TIFF do not. One image
 * at a time, and no operation cache, keep memory predictable.
 */
export function configureDecoder(formats: readonly MediaFormat[]): void {
  sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoad"] });
  sharp.unblock({ operation: formats.map((format) => LOADER[format]) });
  sharp.cache(false);
  sharp.concurrency(1);
}

/**
 * What processing made of an upload. 3d Task 6: `r1`, the scorer's model and score, while a scorer runs and it answered
 * one; absent otherwise, and then the result file carries no score.
 */
export type Processed =
  | { ok: true; width: number; height: number; blurhash: string; small: Buffer; large: Buffer; r1?: { model: string; score: number } }
  | { ok: false; reason: MediaFailure };

const refuse = (reason: MediaFailure): Processed => ({ ok: false, reason });

/** Reads from an open file descriptor without ever loading the whole file. */
function fileReader(fd: number): ByteReader {
  return (offset, length) => {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(length);
    return buffer.subarray(0, readSync(fd, buffer, 0, length, offset));
  };
}

/** The first bytes decide what the file is. No decoder has run when this returns. */
function sniffFile(path: string, formats: readonly MediaFormat[]): { format: MediaFormat } | { reason: MediaFailure } {
  const fd = openSync(path, "r");
  try {
    const read = fileReader(fd);
    const sniffed = sniffImage(read(0, SNIFF_BYTES));
    if (sniffed.kind === "animated") return { reason: "animated_not_supported" };
    if (sniffed.kind !== "image" || !formats.includes(sniffed.format)) return { reason: "unsupported_format" };
    if (sniffed.format === "png" && isAnimatedPng(read)) return { reason: "animated_not_supported" };
    return { format: sniffed.format };
  } finally {
    closeSync(fd);
  }
}

/** What a decoder error means for the person who uploaded the file. A missing input is not their fault and is rethrown. */
function failureOf(err: unknown): MediaFailure {
  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
  if (/input file is missing/i.test(message)) throw err;
  if (/exceeds pixel limit/i.test(message)) return "image_too_large";
  if (/timeout/i.test(message)) return "processing_failed";
  return "corrupt_image";
}

/**
 * Turns one uploaded file into the two WebP sizes and a blurhash, or says why not. The output is a
 * fresh encode: rotated by EXIF, in sRGB, without EXIF, GPS, ICC, XMP, IPTC, thumbnails or gain
 * maps, and without anything that was appended to the file. `failOn: "error"` refuses truncated
 * and broken files but not the harmless libjpeg warnings many phone cameras trigger.
 *
 * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 5 "The adapters" and 10.2): with a scorer, the small size's raw pixels, which are rendered
 * here once for the WebP and the blurhash, are also handed to it, with their width, height and channels; nothing else is.
 */
export async function processImage(path: string, formats: readonly MediaFormat[], scorer: Scorer | null = null): Promise<Processed> {
  const sniffed = sniffFile(path, formats);
  if ("reason" in sniffed) return refuse(sniffed.reason);
  const { format } = sniffed;
  const input = { limitInputPixels: PIXEL_CAP[format], failOn: "error", sequentialRead: true } as const;

  try {
    const meta = await sharp(path, input).metadata();
    if (meta.format !== METADATA_FORMAT[format]) return refuse("unsupported_format");
    if (format === "avif" && meta.compression !== "av1") return refuse("unsupported_format");
    if ((meta.pages ?? 1) > 1) return refuse("animated_not_supported");
    if ((meta.width ?? 0) > MAX_SIDE || (meta.height ?? 0) > MAX_SIDE) return refuse("image_too_large");

    const resized = (edge: number) =>
      sharp(path, input).autoOrient().resize({ width: edge, height: edge, fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true }).timeout({ seconds: 30 });
    const large = await resized(VARIANTS.large.edge).webp({ quality: VARIANTS.large.quality, effort: 4 }).toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

    // The small size is rendered to pixels once. Its WebP and the blurhash both come from those
    // pixels, so neither depends on a decoder: the WebP loader may be switched off.
    const pixels = await resized(VARIANTS.small.edge).toColourspace("srgb").raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
    const raw = { width: pixels.info.width, height: pixels.info.height, channels: pixels.info.channels };
    const small = await sharp(pixels.data, { raw }).webp({ quality: VARIANTS.small.quality, effort: 4 }).timeout({ seconds: 30 }).toBuffer();
    const thumb = await sharp(pixels.data, { raw }).resize(32, 32, { fit: "inside" }).ensureAlpha().raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
    const blurhash = encode(new Uint8ClampedArray(thumb.data), thumb.info.width, thumb.info.height, 4, 3);
    const score = scorer === null ? null : await scorer.score(pixels.data, raw.width, raw.height, raw.channels);

    return { ok: true, width: large.info.width, height: large.info.height, blurhash, small, large: large.data, ...(scorer !== null && score !== null ? { r1: { model: scorer.model, score } } : {}) };
  } catch (err) {
    return refuse(failureOf(err));
  }
}
```

### Replace `infra/compose.yml` (whole file)

```yaml
name: korbat

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "20m", max-file: "5" }

x-node-common: &node-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # 3f Task 5: whether a deletion keeps an account's address, at most seven days, while a report of its sealed images
      # to the authorities is owed. Empty means on; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once.
      REPORT_HOLD: ${API_REPORT_HOLD:-}
      # 3d: the app's site switch, Caddy's (3f), handed to the API too, which refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
      # 3d Task 3: the purge of an image's copies at the edge once it stops being public: off (empty, the default), test
      # (refused while APP_SITE is open) or cloudflare, which needs the zone's id, the API token with the one permission
      # Zone, Cache Purge, and the public hostname images are served under (README, The edge).
      EDGE_PURGE: ${API_EDGE_PURGE:-}
      EDGE_ZONE_ID: ${API_EDGE_ZONE_ID:-}
      EDGE_API_TOKEN: ${API_EDGE_API_TOKEN:-}
      EDGE_HOST: ${API_EDGE_HOST:-}
      # 3d Task 4: whether readers without an account are counted among the recipients, each day's by a keyed digest of
      # the network and the browser's name under a salt that lives 26 hours; on unless set to off (README, The yearly edition).
      RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: ${API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT:-}
      # 3d Task 5: the audit head's daily value. Its outside timestamp: off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or rfc3161, which needs the timestamp authority's https address; and the one address the
      # keeper's daily mail goes to, empty for none (README, The yearly edition).
      HEAD_WITNESS: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS:-}
      HEAD_WITNESS_URL: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL:-}
      HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL: ${API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL:-}
      # 3d Task 6: the R1 check, which the worker reads too (unprefixed): off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or onnx, not in this build; whether a score over the threshold withholds its image (off unless
      # on); and the two days of the owner's impact assessment, empty for none.
      R1_CLASSIFIER: ${R1_CLASSIFIER:-}
      AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      # 3d Task 6: the R1 check's scorer, the API's setting (off when empty), and the site's switch, which the worker reads
      # only to refuse a test scorer while the site is open.
      R1_CLASSIFIER: ${R1_CLASSIFIER:-}
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    # A fixed address on push (3f's review, operations3), which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
    # (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): ntfy lets any one address publish 60 times and then once every 5 seconds (lab
    # L1), which would hold an order's alert behind a flood of contact mail. It lies inside PUSH_SUBNET, at the top of
    # the range, which Docker hands out last; change it, and the file's line, with the subnet.
    networks:
      watch: {}
      push:
        ipv4_address: ${NOTIFY_PUSH_IP:-172.16.91.254}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The hand-over of one seal's files (3f design, sections 5 and 7.14), under the profile handover, started by the operator
  # alone: docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests. The API's
  # image with dist/handover.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no credential, no capability,
  # the image store and (3d) the quarantine read-only, the quarantine looked in first. It has no bind mount here: the
  # directory for the archive is an argument of the command (an empty source would stop every Compose command of the
  # stack), on an encrypted volume owned by uid 1000, the image's user node, the only place it can write. No setting of
  # it is required.
  handover:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["handover"]
    command: ["node", "dist/handover.js"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro

  # The quarantine's mover (3d design, sections 5 and 7.1), under the profile quarantine, started by the operator alone:
  # docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt, with the list that
  # staff.js quarantine-list printed, and the receipt then recorded by staff.js quarantine-record (the README,
  # Quarantine). The API's image with dist/quarantine.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no
  # environment, no credential, no capability and a read-only root; the image store and the quarantine read-write, and
  # nothing else. Its two roots are arguments of its entry point, and it refuses to start without both; what follows the
  # service's name on the command line (--lost, --inventory) is appended to them. It is the one service that writes the
  # quarantine; handover reads it, and the api, migrate and worker services never mount it.
  quarantine:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["quarantine"]
    entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
        # 3f: the terms' contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State; neither is required (Before going public).
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # 3d: the files of images sealed for good, moved out of the store by the quarantine service, on the host's encrypted
  # disk. It is in no backup, by decision: a restore never brings a destroyed file back. Owned by uid 1000, mode 0700, the
  # path the API's image makes (the README, Quarantine and Backups).
  media-quarantine:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

### Replace `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

/** Every non-2xx response from the API has this shape. */
export const ErrorEnvelope = z.object({
  error: z.object({
    code: z.string().min(1),
    message: z.string().min(1),
    requestId: z.string().optional(),
    details: z.unknown().optional(),
  }),
});
export type ErrorEnvelope = z.infer<typeof ErrorEnvelope>;

export const CheckState = z.enum(["ok", "fail"]);

export const HealthResponse = z.object({
  status: z.enum(["ok", "degraded"]),
  version: z.string(),
  checks: z.record(z.string(), CheckState),
});
export type HealthResponse = z.infer<typeof HealthResponse>;

/** Keyset pagination query params shared by every list endpoint. */
export const Pagination = z.object({
  cursor: z.string().min(1).max(200).optional(),
  limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(20),
});
export type Pagination = z.infer<typeof Pagination>;
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

// Moderation cases (3c design, section 10): the constants and digests that the database, the API, the console, the app,
// the mails and the terms share. Each is the one source its words and numbers are taken from. This module imports
// nothing from staff.ts, and the index evaluates it first, so staff.ts can read these constants while it loads; an import
// the other way round would be a cycle that fails at load. For the same reason it imports nothing from social.ts, whose
// shapes may come to name this module's constants: what a notice needs of a post's id and of a handle is written here.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- rules, categories and keywords

 * Commission removes stays here: a kept row may hold it, and only the lists offered for new input drop it.
 */
export const TDB_CATEGORIES = [
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
] as const;
export type TdbCategory = (typeof TDB_CATEGORIES)[number];

/** The two categories a notifier never chooses: a rule-only report gets the first, a notifier who is not sure the second. */
type UnofferedCategory = "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" | "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE";
export type TdbFormCategory = Exclude<TdbCategory, UnofferedCategory>;

/** The 14 categories the illegal-ground form shows. */
export const TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES: readonly TdbFormCategory[] = TDB_CATEGORIES.filter(
  (category): category is TdbFormCategory => category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" && category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
);

/**
 * The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material and the Transparency Database keyword each stores. "abuse"
 * stores none: the database has no keyword for it.
 */
export const CSAM_KEYWORDS = {
  csam: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL",
  deepfake: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE",
  grooming: "KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS",
  abuse: null,
} as const;
export type CsamKeywordChoice = keyof typeof CSAM_KEYWORDS;

/** The keywords a decision on the law may carry: in 3c only the Transparency Database's "Terrorist content". */
export const DECISION_KEYWORDS = ["KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT"] as const;
export type DecisionKeyword = (typeof DECISION_KEYWORDS)[number];

/** The category the composer presets for a decision under each rule. */
export const RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY = {
  R1: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  R2: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  R3: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  R4: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  R5: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
  R6: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
} as const satisfies Record<RuleId, TdbCategory>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- lanes

/** The queue's lanes: 0 is the most urgent. A case takes the most severe lane of its unanswered items. */
export type Lane = 0 | 1 | 2;

/** R2 and R5 are urgent; R3 and R4 come next; R1 and R6 last. */
const RULE_LANES: Record<RuleId, Lane> = { R1: 2, R2: 0, R3: 1, R4: 1, R5: 0, R6: 2 };

/** The categories that are not in lane 2: violence, public security and self-harm are urgent; six more come next. */
const CATEGORY_LANES: Partial<Record<TdbCategory, Lane>> = {
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE: 1,
};

/**
 * The lane of an intake's items, from its ground alone: nothing is weighted. The CSAM path is urgent whatever else is
 * said. Otherwise it is the more severe of the cited rule's lane and, on a notice that alleges illegality, the category's:
 * only there is the category a claim about the content, where on a rule report or a finding it is korbat's own
 * classification for the Transparency Database.
 */
export function laneFor(input: { ruleId: RuleId | null; allegesIllegal: boolean; csam: boolean; category: TdbCategory }): Lane {
  if (input.csam) return 0;
  const byRule: Lane = input.ruleId === null ? 2 : RULE_LANES[input.ruleId];
  const byCategory: Lane = input.allegesIllegal ? (CATEGORY_LANES[input.category] ?? 2) : 2;
  return byRule < byCategory ? byRule : byCategory;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- limits and periods

/**

} as const;

/** A notice on the CSAM path names at most one account: one such target reaches every image on the account's posts. */

/** How many months back a case page counts earlier answers to reports of this kind about the same target or author. */

/** How many rows of a seal's list the case answer carries. */

export const APPEAL_MONTHS = 6;

/** Appeals a day per account, and re-examinations a day per account or network. */
export const DAILY_LIMITS = { appeals: 5, reexaminations: 5 } as const;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- account sanctions (3e design, section 10.1)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- measures

/**
 * The ledger's kinds, in the order of the database's action_kind: 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six
 * measures (a strike, a suspension, a termination, a retired handle, a warning about reporting and a restriction of it)
 * and four reversals (3e design, section 10.1); then 3f's measure of an authority's order and its reversal (3f design,
 * section 10.1), which only an order decision and its correction hold.
 */
export const ACTION_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",

  "unseal_media",
  "restore_media",

  "disable_by_order",
  "reinstate_by_order",
] as const;

/**
 * What a measure acts on: a post, one image of it, every image its case reaches, one of an account's two fields, the
 * account itself (a strike, a suspension or a termination), its handle, or its reports under the rules.
 */
export type MeasureTarget = "post" | "image" | "images" | "display_name" | "bio" | "account" | "handle" | "reporting";

export interface MeasureSpec {
  /** A decision taken while deciding (interim) may hold it. */
  interim: boolean;
  /** A decision that decides the case (final) may hold it. */
  final: boolean;
  /** For a reversal, the measures it lifts (it names exactly one row of them); null for a measure. */
  lifts: readonly ActionKind[] | null;
  target: MeasureTarget;
  /** The words for it in the composer, the statement and the terms. */
  label: string;
}

 */
export const MEASURES = {
  withhold: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Withhold the post" },
  remove: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Remove" },
  seal_media: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "images", label: "Seal the images this case reaches" },

  remove_media: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Remove one image" },

  reset_bio: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "bio", label: "Reset bio" },
  restore: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold", "remove"], target: "post", label: "Lift the restriction of the post" },
  unseal_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["seal_media"], target: "images", label: "Lift the seal" },
  restore_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold_media", "remove_media"], target: "image", label: "Lift the restriction of one image" },
  restore_display_name: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_display_name"], target: "display_name", label: "Lift the reset of the display name" },
  restore_bio: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_bio"], target: "bio", label: "Lift the reset of the bio" },
  // 3e (design, section 18, W.1). Each measure of 3e is taken only when the case is decided, and none while deciding.
  strike: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Strike" },
  suspend: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Suspend the account" },
  terminate: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Terminate the account" },
  retire_handle: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "handle", label: "Retire the handle" },
  warn_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Warn about reporting" },
  restrict_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Restrict reporting" },
  overrule: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["strike"], target: "account", label: "Overrule the strike" },
  lift_suspension: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["suspend", "terminate"], target: "account", label: "Lift the suspension" },
  unretire_handle: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["retire_handle"], target: "handle", label: "Give the handle back" },
  lift_reporting: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"], target: "reporting", label: "Lift the reporting measure" },

  disable_by_order: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Disabled for an order" },

/** The fourteen measures and the ten reversals, each list in the ledger's order: what a statement's data keeps apart. */
export const MEASURE_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
  "disable_by_order",
] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];

export const REVERSAL_KINDS = ["restore", "unseal_media", "restore_media", "restore_display_name", "restore_bio", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting", "reinstate_by_order"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];

/**
 * The console's fixed drafts of the facts and the reason of a seal (3c design, section 10). Nobody at korbat opens images
 * that are reported as child sexual abuse material, so none of these says or implies that korbat found them to be such
 * material, and each reason says that korbat's staff do not open them: the statement then tells its author what korbat
 * knows and no more. The composer fills them in, and the moderator may edit them. The two `added` drafts are for a case
 * whose suspect items korbat added for a quoted post: they never say that this post was reported, and name no other post.
```
